And it gives companies the legal certainty to be able to do just that without monstrous bureaucracy."" This would ""necessarily include a modernization of the Working Hours Act"". Digitalization offers more and more people the opportunity to decide for themselves where and when they want to work. ""But if you want to read a business e-mail at 10 or 11 p.m. today, you must not return to work before 10 a.m. the next day. That is out of touch with reality, hardly anyone adheres to it anymore."" Germany should be guided here by the EU directive on working time. This prescribes the same weekly working hours and break times as German law, but allows a more flexible schedule during the week. The CDU/CSU and SPD were accused by the FDP parliamentary group's labor market spokesman of talking past each other on this point. Economics Minister Peter Altmaier (CDU) and the CDU/CSU would prefer not to change anything at all. Labor Minister Hubertus Heil (SPD) and the SPD ""are forging ahead and announcing a law, but so far there is only a headline"". It is to be feared that the SPD simply wants to continue old rules from the analog world into the digital age or create one-sided legal claims. However, the coronavirus pandemic shows that mobile working is possible in many places and in many professions - even where there was previously skepticism. ""This offers us great opportunities even after the crisis: less traffic, a very short commute to work, more flexibility in terms of where you work and therefore more self-determination for everyone."" But it is also clear: ""Not everyone can and wants to work from home all the time."" Vogel referred to the experience of the neighboring Netherlands. They have been showing us how it's done for five years now: in one package, the Working Hours Act was modernized, home office and working in a café were made equally possible and a right to discussion was introduced for employees. Mobile working is no longer particularly necessary to justify, but rather to reject.

30 percent less emissions by 2030: EU agrees on climate protection targets for trucks and buses Following in the footsteps of car manufacturers, the EU is now also setting CO2 targets for truck and bus manufacturers. However, the conditions are not as strict as the European Parliament had hoped. For the first time, the EU is imposing strict climate protection requirements on truck and bus manufacturers. Negotiators from the member states and the European Parliament agreed on Tuesday night that the average carbon dioxide emissions of new vehicles must be 30 percent lower from 2030 than in 2019. An interim target of 15 percent is to be introduced for 2025. At the same time, there are plans to create new incentives for the use of zero-emission and low-emission vehicles, as the EU Commission confirmed on Tuesday morning. Details of the provisional agreement were not initially disclosed. According to a spokesperson for the Council of Member States, they should be published in the course of the day. The vehicle manufacturers had tried to prevent the new regulations until the very end. Among other things, they argue that alternative drive systems such as electric motors are difficult to implement in long-distance transportation. The EU member states and the European Parliament had already agreed on new climate targets for cars last December. Carbon dioxide emissions from new cars are set to fall by 37.5 percent by 2030 compared to 2021. The fact that the new requirements for truck and bus manufacturers are less strict than those for cars is due to the fact that buyers of trucks and buses generally pay much more attention to low fuel consumption than those of cars in order to maximize profits. This in turn means that commercial vehicle manufacturers tend to produce vehicles with optimized fuel consumption and therefore do not have quite as much savings potential. Nevertheless, the EU Parliament had actually called for more ambitious targets for heavy commercial vehicles as well. It wanted a 35 percent reduction in CO2 levels by 2030 and an interim target of 20 percent by 2025. Bas Eickhout, the Dutch Green politician and responsible rapporteur of the European Parliament, criticized the member states on Tuesday. ""Germany, Italy and some central European countries in particular have blocked stronger climate targets,"" he said. In the long term, this would not only harm the climate, but also European industry. Nevertheless, Eickhout described the agreement as a great success. The regulation will help to reduce pollution on the roads and improve air quality, he commented. The responsible EU Commissioner Miguel Arias Cañete also welcomed the agreement. This completes the legal framework that should enable the EU climate protection targets to be achieved, he said. They envisage a reduction in greenhouse gas emissions of at least 40 percent by 2030 compared to 1990 levels.

Nightmares in neo-noir ""It's hard to be so precise about something so crazy."" The script that director Alice (Ayelet Zurer) has in her hands is quite something. The scenes described in it are obviously explicitly overwhelming and threatening. Alice had ignored the script in her email inbox for two weeks, until on the train home - was it really a coincidence? - got to know the author. The young Sophie (Lihi Koronowski) has outed herself as an admirer of her work and was allegedly even on one of Alice's earlier writing courses. Now Room 209, as the title suggests, is to be made into a movie. Once home, she tells her husband David (Gal Toren), a popular actor, about the strange encounter with the stranger on the train. He knows the book because he is already engaged as the male lead. ""Pretty perverse,"" he says. It is the story of a young woman who begins an S&M relationship with the father of her best friend - with fatal consequences. Alice finishes reading Room 209 the same night. Can you make something like that up? Alice is in her late forties, has three daughters and a beautiful house on the outskirts of the city. A normal, well-off family life, you might think - but why is the mother-in-law constantly visiting and making unsubtle claims of ownership over her son? At one point, she wears her daughter-in-law's silk nightgown. Alice goes through a creative crisis, shoots television commercials, can no longer write. She knows that Room 209 would save her as a director. What she doesn't know is that Sophie has long since chosen her. Because the young author is suddenly always there, appears at the children's birthday party and paints Alice's little daughter deep red lips. She secretly meets the actress who is to play the lead role on the eve of the audition, whereupon she bursts into tears during the audition. Positions herself for the role and - like the young woman in her own book - has an older boyfriend. And like Room 209, Losing Alice is about desire right from the start. About obsession. It's about playing with the power you have over other people. Perhaps also about the girlfriend, when she no longer knows how to help herself and - as can be seen in the first few minutes of this series, which is disturbing from the start - seeks redemption in a hotel room. Losing Alice is one of the most unusual TV series these days and comes - once again - from Israel. Released last summer in Israel and now internationally by Apple TV+, the eight-part thriller is unlike most series productions in that it comes from a single source - and is therefore more reminiscent of classic auteur cinema. Sigal Avin, who was born in Florida and emigrated to Israel with her parents at the age of ten, has created a scenario as screenwriter and director in which psycho-horror, neo-noir nightmares and social studies merge into one another. It is her own world that becomes a threat to Alice, her own constraints and unfulfilled desires. Much of it seems familiar, or at least as familiar as the films of Alfred Hitchcock, Brian De Palma and David Lynch, some of which are even quoted directly. But you don't need to be familiar with the numerous allusions to soon feel rather uncomfortable on the false ground on which you are being led: Is this a fiction of an unusual TV series feigned as reality, as usual? Are the flashbacks and flashforwards that repeatedly take us by surprise fragments of Alice's past or eerie visions of the future? Or is it already footage from Room 209, as Alice imagines this movie to be? Sigal Avin's astonishing skill also lies in the way she allows her heroine to walk open-eyed into her doom: Although every suspicion that arises in Alice is subsequently proven to be true, her resistance to the intruder grows weaker from episode to episode. Her and David's hallucinations and fantasies intertwine like an endlessly woven ribbon with the story of Sophie, a femme fatale with a pageboy head who sets one trap after another for them. At least that's what they think. Until you realize that you have landed in one yourself while watching.

Cosmetics are the beginning of all boosters This choice is the best choice of an ""Anglicism of the Year"". This decision makes it easy to forget how unsatisfactory the outdated word choices of all kinds have long been. In their efforts to be correct, they stand in the way of anything that could lead to some kind of insight through originality or exposure. Because criticism suffices in pointing to something that is either very right or very wrong. This is no different with ""boosters"". Nevertheless! Unlike the noun, which is clearly borrowed from English, the verb is probably a German creation of its own, according to the press release issued by the jury headed by linguist Anatol Stefanowitsch. The noun booster shot stands for ""booster vaccination"", and that really doesn't sound catchy. The corresponding verb is actually ""to boost"", but since the beginning of January ""to booster"" has been used more frequently in English. What a booster for the self-confidence of the ""German language community"", because they ""recognized the potential of English well before the English language community and used it for themselves"". Too woke to be clear. For yourself? More for an idea. A look at the finalists reveals this: ""Long Covid"", ""QR code"", ""cringe"", ""woke"". All somehow just the green around the flower. ""Boosting"" is exclusively for the good and sounds only half as infantile as ""spades"" and nowhere near as pretentious as ""pimping"" or - you're already looking at a smart person with a smart hairstyle: ""spicing up"". The Digital Dictionary of the German Language would boost when it comes to stimulating, reinforcing, magnifying, just for example an immune reaction. Cosmetics were the beginning of all boosters. Lips and eyelashes can be boosted for a long time. Products such as ""Natucollagen Boost Volume Lip Serum"" and ""Mascara med Ultra Boost"" boost business and well-being in general, as long as this is fed by the kind of plumping and puffing that invigorates all linguistic fashions. Language criticism as a campaign booster. The message can be even more important than the text, the resonance even more important than the sound. In contrast to the word ""booster vaccination"", the jury said that ""booster"" enables ""concise yet clear communication"" in the ""ongoing pandemic"". Because things have to move quickly if the laboratories can no longer keep up, not to mention the federal and state governments. Secondly, the emphasis is - attention, message: ""on the transience of vaccination protection - we are only boosted as long as the protective effect of the booster vaccination is still sufficiently high."" Language criticism as a campaign booster. Thirdly, such a beautiful word is a mirror to itself. It has ""an optimistic and dynamic connotation"", the reasoning goes, ""which the refresh simply cannot match"". It would not be fair to accuse the jury of voluntary satire at this point. Because the fun naturally stops when it comes to vaccination, which leads to interesting effects. Since what must not be said cannot be funny, the comic is concentrated in the overtones of what is said. Or as they say today: the joke boosts the joke.

Culture ""Dangerous"" art: Rosemarie Trockel in Frankfurt The entrance hall of Frankfurt's Museum of Modern Art features a circumferential frieze of a blue, knitted-looking pattern that appears strangely regular despite its perforated stretching. Like a delicate barrier that could rise into the air in the next moment. ""Prisoner of yourself"" is the title of this work, which has been screen-printed directly onto the museum wall. Rosemarie Trockel seems to say that my image as a knitting artist has haunted me for a long time; I am a victim of my success. But it's not that bad. Could be a leitmotif for us all, says Susanne Pfeffer, director of the house: ""That we are all caught up in ourselves, in our own identity, in our gender, in our culture. That it is actually a lifelong task to break out of these structures, which are often very rigid and violent."" Stove top reliefs and knitting pictures. In a nearby film, Rosemarie Trockel has captured herself and interrogates her doppelganger with the question: ""Who is the best artist?"". And it takes a long time, forced by physical and psychological abuse, before the interviewee finally answers: ""Rosemarie Trockel"". The artist has been walking this fine line between prejudice, self-observation, social values and defiant self-assertion for many decades: sleepwalkingly confident and delightfully humorous. Naturally, many of her knitting pictures with the wool seal ornament can be seen in Frankfurt. Or her stove-top reliefs, which mock the expected sphere of female creativity. Two of them are connected to a socket, the plates become hot and start to glow, creating a whole new dimension of ""dangerous"" art. In the course of her career, Rosemarie Trockel has developed a wide range of tools to undermine and satirize social roles. Perpetrator? Victims? ""There is a work called 'Misleading Interpretation', where you can see her, a photo of her, but her eyes are covered with a black bar and her nose is bleeding and her hair is all wet,"" says Susanne Pfeffer. Ask yourself: has she just been a victim of violence or has she herself been violent? And she believes that this is also a fundamental question posed by Rosemarie Trockel: that it is sometimes impossible to tell when we are perpetrators and when we are victims. Large ceramic wall reliefs are particularly impressive. They look strangely metallic and are actually reminiscent of the surface texture of vegetable graters that women love to cut their fingers on. ""That's what makes her very unique formal language, that she always tries to go against the mainstream and use a material about which the experts say: that's not how it works,"" says Pfeffer. Room for ambivalence. At a time when the gender debate is becoming increasingly rigid, this extremely comprehensive exhibition of Rosemarie Trockel's work is delightfully liberal. Of course, the artist fights against the grandiose pathetic gestures of the male world of artists, but her work has truly not exhausted itself in this. If you allow ambivalences, says Susanne Pfeffer, you cannot look at people solely from the gender context. ""A person is not just a woman, not just a man, not just a child. So that's also very important for her. A person is also always many things. And you can also see and perceive it in very different ways. But allowing that to happen is really important to her. The magnificently presented exhibition ends with a glass cube in which square-cut pieces of knitted pictures are layered on top of each other. An ironic cross-reference to the pathos of minimal art, but also a relieved farewell to its clichéd reputation. When you see the display cases in which Rosemarie Trockel celebrates natural art forms - leaves, seed pods, dried flowers - then you finally realize that this artist keeps her eyes wide open and always knows how to find new ways to find inspiration.

Fast with a pen: 17-year-old creates films and comics Drawing, writing, designing animated films, making music and recording albums - David Wiechert's talents would be enough for several creative minds. Maisach - The 17-year-old devotes himself to his many projects from morning to night. His biggest dream is to one day earn real money with his drawing and design skills - and ideally to combine them all. The first client contacted David Wiechert via the school. Those responsible at the Hans Stangl Foundation in Jesenwang found out about the young artist from a report in the Tagblatt newspaper. David was only 13 at the time, but had already produced his first comic book, taken part in comic festivals, sold pictures at markets and won second place in the district's youth art competition. For the Hans Stangl Foundation, he was asked to create a 2D animated film with a self-designed bee to illustrate the foundation's work. PC from the recycling center. A huge task for which the teenager did not even have the right equipment. Because his old PC from the recycling center was not equipped with the appropriate software, the foundation gave him a new device. David taught himself the elaborate animation program. He spent months drawing one picture after another on paper - because every tiny movement of the figures required a new picture - and finally filmed everything with his camera. The film can still be seen today on the foundation's homepage. The ""KorBienian"" bee buzzes around children, senior citizens and athletes or stands at the blackboard as a teacher - because the foundation supports youth and elderly care, sport, education, art and culture. The movie is even accompanied by an appropriate whirring sound. Comic book. The 17-year-old now owns a drawing tablet and creates small animated films within a day - that's how fast he is with the pen. ""If we didn't see it with our own eyes, we wouldn't believe it,"" say his parents Thomas and Anja Wiechert. But some things do take longer - David's latest comic book, for example. It is his fifth and, at almost 200 pages, his largest project. ""I've been working on this for several months,"" he says. It's a story about wolves, archaic and a little dark. By the way: Everything from the region is now also available in our regular inspiration the young author gets from the Internet or from his great role model H.P.. Lovecraft, an American writer who is considered the most important representative of fantastic horror literature of the 20th century. century. David also makes music on the side. ""I play guitar, flute and harmonica,"" he says. Using real DJ programs, he mixes the sounds together and creates his own animation for each one. He has already recorded 60 songs. Animation studio? But how do you turn all this into a sustainable career? David has already completed an internship at a film editing company. But it was boring, because he only had to optimize the colors and tones of foreign films. That's not for him in the long term. He does not want to work on the brainchildren of others, but rather create things ""that arise from my mind"". David graduated from Dorothea-von-Haldenberg-Schule in Mammendorf last year as one of the best students. He could now attend the Fachoberschule (FOS) for design - he has already passed the entrance exam. ""But I don't actually want to go to school anymore,"" he says. ""I would like to learn something else, but the FOS is too unspecific for me."" He would much rather work in an animation studio, where he would like to be as artistically and technically challenged as possible. And preferably also write screenplays.

40 years of ""I want fun"" ""Petrol for three marks ten"" Millions can sing along to it: the Neue Deutsche Welle song ""Ich will Spaß"" by Markus. The song was a number one hit 40 years ago. In June 1982, the song about an enthusiastic car driver entered the charts, and in August it spent two weeks at the top position in Germany. The lyrics read, among other things: ""And even if gas costs three marks ten, it won't matter, it'll be fine! I want to drive!"". 40 years later, the fuel price that was sung about as a horror back then would have felt like a bargain. Right? The vocal ego of ""Ich will Spaß"" fills up on super: ""Will nicht spar'n, will nicht vernünftig sein, tank nur das gute Super rein"". He drives an Italian luxury sports car and is against any speed limit: ""My Maserati goes two hundred and ten; poof, the police didn't see it"". And at the petrol station, the man from ""I want fun"" is a welcome customer: ""The petrol station attendant is my best friend; ooh, when I come, how happy he is"". Consumer prices have doubled According to the ADAC, a liter of Super cost an average of 1.40 marks in 1982. Today, the price board at the filling station shows an average of around 2.20 euros for a liter of E10. However, price comparisons between the DM era and today's euro era are difficult, partly because the conversion rate fixed on New Year's Eve 1998 (1 euro = 1.95583 Deutschmarks) was based exactly on the value of the German currency at that time in relation to the other euro currencies. But this much can already be said: the price defined as a horror vision in the song has not yet been reached, even after the price jumps following the start of the war in Ukraine. Considering that the consumer price level has roughly doubled since 1982, the 3.10 marks accepted by singer Markus back then would correspond to a price of around 6.20 marks today ? or the equivalent of 3.17 euros. Nevertheless, the high price of fuel naturally hurts many drivers, especially as it is largely made up of taxes. ""Ich will Spaß"" singer Markus has a clear opinion on the current fuel prices. He is ""actually in favor of a fuel price brake"", as he said when asked by dpa. ""For me personally, it should be 1.55 euros, because that would be 3.10 DM divided by two,"" says the singer, who was born in Bad Camberg in Hesse and is now 62 years old. He appeals: ""Dear Federal Government, at least temporarily reduce ? Similar to the coronavirus crisis - taxes."" Then there will still be enough money for the state, he says. A song describes an attitude to life Markus' ""Ich will Spaß"" is one of the biggest Neue Deutsche Welle hits ever. Time and again, it is also used as a general motto for the attitude to life of (male) youth. Another success for Markus was the duet ""Kleine Taschenlampe brenn'"" with Nena. Markus played the leading role alongside Nena in the movie ""Gib Gas, ich will Spaß"" (1983). In recent years, Mörl has appeared repeatedly as a singer and also on television. Five years ago, he and his partner Yvonne König, now 50, took part in the RTL reality show ""Das Sommerhaus der Stars ? Battle of the Celebrity Couples"". In summer 2020, Markus and Yvonne got married on a Rhine boat live on television (RTLzwei). In 2021 he released the single ""Helden"" and in 2022 the hit ""Herzschlag"". A new album is due to be released in the summer - entitled: ""Life loves me... and I love life"".

New target of pro-Kremlin propagandists"": Russian campaign is likely to turn Germans against Ukrainians The war in Ukraine is also an information war in which the warring parties want to achieve their goals with propaganda. Russia has now apparently identified German internet users as the cause. According to the Russian media, Ukrainian refugees are causing downright chaos in the host countries. Vandalized trains, arson, targeted benefit fraud, terror. At first glance, such reports seem authentic. That has a system. The Kremlin has been using targeted propaganda for years. A video recently circulated claiming that Ukrainian refugees had torched a house in an attempt to set fire to a Russian flag. The video showed the ""Bild"" logo. But it had nothing at all to do with the clip. A similar story was reported by t-online in the summer. Pro-Russian videos using the portal's logo circulated on the internet. Codes from German media were technically integrated and even entire websites were copied. ""After clicking on a link, the environment appears deceptively real,"" the report said. ""The articles you read there and the videos you can watch with the logo of the media brands are clearly pro-Russian propaganda."" This type of disinformation is most likely part of a larger Russian strategy. ""We are in times of hybrid warfare,"" Austrian EU politician Lukas Mandl (ÖVP) recently told IPPEN.MEDIA . This refers to a type of war that involves not only traditional military means, but also attacks via the internet, be it hacker attacks or targeted disinformation campaigns. The Federal Ministry of Defense is aware of this danger. As early as 2016, it warned of ""disinformation as a means of hybrid warfare"" - and saw a targeted Russian campaign. ""Through so-called internet trolls and politically controlled media campaigns, the Kremlin is trying to influence the media, politics and public opinion in Western societies."" This was demonstrated six years ago when Russian media reported on a 13-year-old girl from Berlin. The daughter of German-Russian parents returned home the day after she was reported missing and told her parents that she had been raped by three southern men. As it soon turned out, this was a lie. Nevertheless, Russia-affiliated media such as RT (formerly Russia Today) and Sputnik picked up the story, embellished it as they saw fit and accused the German authorities of a cover-up. Russian propaganda is currently directed primarily against Ukrainians who have fled to Europe. Officially, there are 7.9 million people. from a ""new target of pro-Kremlin propagandists"": Turning Europeans against Ukrainians who have fled. Germany is ""at the center of Moscow's information campaign"". Russia is relying on fake internet posts, which Mark Zuckerberg's tech giant Meta describes as ""the largest and most complex Russian operation since the beginning of the war"". It is not yet clear whether this goal will be achieved. ""Lies about Ukrainian refugees and attempts to capitalize on Europeans' fears have not yet successfully polarized or shaped public discourse,"" according to a recent study by the European Policy Center supported by the European Parliament. But the proportion of information hostile to Ukrainian refugees ""is increasing and generating greater engagement on social media,"" the study warned. Some false claims can be quickly refuted. For example, it quickly became clear that it was not Ukrainian refugees who were rioting on a regional train, but FC Augsburg fans. Fact checks help to clear up fake news, but are by no means the last word in wisdom: studies show that a) they are read by significantly fewer people than the original false claim, which in turn b) is also so successful because fake news in social media actually benefits from the algorithm. This also benefits Russian propaganda.

Germany prepares for scenarios in the Ukraine conflict: ""Should it come to an invasion ..."" The German security authorities are preparing for ""every scenario"" in view of the Ukraine-Russia conflict. You are looking to exchange ideas with other EU countries. Berlin - What impact will the conflict between Russia and Ukraine have on Germany? The German security authorities are also concerned about this. ""The situation is extremely tense,"" the Federal Minister of the Interior told the Funke Mediengruppe newspapers. And the SPD politician is also a little more specific: ""That's why we are preparing for every scenario and are very vigilant. This applies to the protection of facilities in Germany, to the defense against cyber threats and to possible refugee movements towards our neighboring countries."" In view of the Russian troop deployment in the border region with Ukraine, the West fears that the deployment of tens of thousands of soldiers could serve to prepare for war. Russia has vehemently rejected this for weeks. The current conflict is also the dominant topic at the Munich Security Conference - even though Russia, of all countries, is staying away this year. Foreign Minister Annalena Baerbock gave a remarkable speech on Friday in which she also got personal. The Westdeutsche Allgemeine Zeitung also quotes security circles: Should an invasion occur, migration movements, initially within Ukraine, but also in particular to neighboring countries, cannot be ruled out. At present, however, there are still no indications of increased migration movements to Germany."" Conflict over Ukraine: wave of refugees to the EU possible. In view of the growing tensions, the EU has already warned of possible refugee flows into the countries of the European Union: ""It is estimated that between 20,000 and more than one million refugees could arrive,"" said the Vice-President of the EU Commission, Margaritis Schinas, with a view to a possible military escalation in the world. Since Poland, for example, has a long border with Ukraine, many people are looking there. ""We are monitoring the situation in Ukraine very closely and are in close contact with the federal government, the federal states, the EU Commission and the other EU member states,"" continued Interior Minister Faeser. Ukraine conflict: Biden convinced of Putin's decision to invade. US President Joe Biden said on Friday (18. February), he was ""convinced"" that Russian President Vladimir Putin had made the decision to invade neighboring Ukraine. ""We have reasons to believe that the Russian military is planning and intending to attack Ukraine in the coming week, in the coming days."" He added: ""We believe they will attack the Ukrainian capital Kiev, a city of 2.8 million innocent people.""

Biden remains skeptical - USA plays out Russian invasion on the drawing board There is movement in the Ukraine showdown - and in the struggle between war and peace in Europe, there has recently been hope of a last-minute diplomatic solution. The Russian Ministry of Defense recently announced the end of the manoeuvre in Crimea. Nevertheless, US President Joe Biden remains skeptical and warned of a possible Russian invasion of Ukraine in a televised address on Tuesday evening. ""We are ready to respond decisively to a Russian attack on Ukraine, which is still very clearly a possibility,"" Biden made clear. Biden responded cautiously to an announcement by the Russian Ministry of Defense to withdraw some troops. ""That would be good, but we haven't verified it yet,"" said the US President. ""We have not yet verified that Russian military units are returning to their bases."" Rather, US analysts have concluded that the Russian armed forces are still in a ""threatening position"". And Washington is obviously prepared for this. As has now become known, the White House had set up a separate advisory group to draw up strategies and plans for multiple war scenarios and their consequences. Name of the group: ""Tiger Team"". At the table were experts, military advisors and government representatives, including from the State Department and the Departments of Energy, Treasury and Homeland Security. War scenarios should have been played out in every detail - from strategic, limited troop advances to a complete war of conquest by Russian forces following a possible order to attack by Kremlin ruler Vladimir Putin. These included the occupation of the country and the removal of the elected President Volodymyr Selensky. The team sat together for hours and played out an invasion of the Eastern European country day by day. The ""Tiger Team"" was set up within the National Security Council, the most important advisory body to US President Joe Biden, back in October, when the first troop movements towards the Ukrainian border were observed by intelligence services. Reason for the planning games: The White House wanted to avoid a fiasco similar to the one in Afghanistan, when the US withdrawal in the midst of the Taliban victory campaign turned into bloody chaos and 13 US soldiers died in a terrorist attack. ""Our hope is still that there is a diplomatic way to avoid all of this so that we never have to implement our concepts, our playbook,"" Jonathan Finer, Biden's deputy national security adviser, told The Washington Post. ""But it's about making sure we're ready if and when we need to be! ""

Discussion on the war in Ukraine: ""We Europeans are stronger than Putin because we are democracies"" There are anniversaries that should not exist. One such date is 24. February, when the Russian war of aggression in Ukraine began. To mark the occasion, the city of Saarbrücken organized a discussion in the town hall with participants Lesya Matiyuk from the citizens' initiative UkraineFreundeSaar, Alexander Friedman from the Chair of European Contemporary History at Saarland University and Lord Mayor Uwe Conradt (CDU). Sabine Dengel (SPD), Head of Cultural Affairs, introduced and moderated the event. It initially condemned Russia's invasion as a ""war of aggression without reason"". The whole situation has also presented the city of Saarbrücken with major challenges. Before the discussion, Friedman gave a keynote speech and began with the victims of the war, the youngest of whom was only two days old. There are now around 200,000 Russian soldiers killed and around 100,000 Ukrainian soldiers. ""This is the price for the phantom pains and imperial dreams of Soviet Union nostalgics,"" the Belarusian historian noted. The invasion of Ukraine is a prologue to an even bigger war, possibly a world war. From Friedman's point of view, the talk of ""Putin's war"" has been a Western and especially German wishful thinking from the very beginning, which unfortunately has little to do with reality. The majority of Russians are still firmly behind their president, either out of conviction or indoctrinated by propaganda. ""So this is Russia's war,"" said Friedman. Demands for a renunciation of arms deliveries and compromises at the expense of Ukraine were evidence of political naivety. He ended his short lecture with the exclamation ""Slava Ukrajini"", ""Glory to Ukraine"", which was popularized by Ukrainian President Volodymyr Selenskyj. Dengel then wanted to know from Friedman whether Russia would use nuclear weapons. This cannot be ruled out, as Putin has his back to the wall. On the other hand, Russian propaganda is deliberately threatening to stir up fear in the West. Matiyuk, who comes from southern Ukraine and holds a doctorate in German studies, was asked about the situation of Ukrainian refugees in Saarland. There are around 15,000 to 16,000 of them and they often feel very torn between their old and new homes. ""How do they perceive the German aid services? "", Dengel wanted to know. Matiyuk stated that the Ukrainians could not understand the hesitant attitude of the German government, especially after masses of girls had been raped shortly after the start of the war. Of course, the image that the Russians get of the Germans through their state media is far worse, said Friedman. It describes the continuity of Germany from the Third Reich to the current Federal Republic. Calling others Nazis is a trademark of Russian propaganda. ""The world is very simple from their point of view. It consists of good people who are not Nazis. But those who condemn Russia's policies are all Nazis."" Political broadcasts discuss in which German city it would be best to deploy nuclear weapons. Saarbrücken is not mentioned, but the US base at Ramstein is. According to Friedman, Putin is not interested in negotiations, which is why he thinks little of the appeal by Sarah Wagenknecht and Alice Schwarzer calling for them. However, Russia needs a breather in order to modernize its own army. The scientist from Saarland University said that we were probably dealing with a long, bloody war and compared it to the eight-year Iran-Iraq war 40 years ago. Matiyuk reported on the aid deliveries that she organizes from the Saarland with her association. Ukrainians are very self-critical and know that there is still a lot of corruption in the country, she said. For this reason, they are looking very closely at where the aid, such as power generators, is going. In addition, the company makes targeted enquiries with institutional partners in order to be able to supply what is actually needed. Mayor Conradt gave the closing speech. He called for more financial support for local authorities to help refugees. Less bureaucracy is also needed. As far as Russia was concerned, one had to ask oneself whether we had not collectively looked the other way for a long time, especially with regard to economic relations. ""What was so unimaginable on 24. February, if you knew Putin? "", asked the mayor, referring to Georgia, Crimea and the destabilization of eastern Ukraine. With regard to China as a trading partner, Conradt also said that we could not go on like this. For Ukraine, it is about peace and freedom. ""I think we all need to make another effort. Life in freedom is a permanent battle against the forces that fight against freedom. I am firmly convinced that we Europeans are stronger than Putin because we are democracies.""

Tensions in the Gulf region: Norwegian ship ""hit by object"" in the Gulf of Oman The Norwegian-flagged oil tanker ""Andrea Victory"" was mysteriously damaged in the Gulf of Oman on Sunday morning. The tanker had been hit by ""an unknown object"", a spokesman for the maritime service provider Thome Ship Management told the German Press Agency. ""The crew on board is safe and sound. There is damage, but the ship is stable,"" he said. The tanker was anchored in the Emirate of Fujairah at the time. Fujairah is located on one of the world's most important waterways for oil exports. The authorities of the United Arab Emirates (UAE) had previously reported ""anti-state operations"" against four ships in the region. Saudi Arabia's energy minister, Chalid al-Falih, said that two Saudi oil tankers had been severely damaged in a ""sabotage attack"". The exact circumstances remained mysterious. There were initially no details or independent confirmation of the alleged incidents on Monday. According to information from the Saudi-affiliated TV station Al-Arabija, the other two ships came from the United Arab Emirates and Norway. The small emirate of Fujairah is located in the east of the UAE on the Gulf of Oman, which separates the Arabian Peninsula and Iran. One of the world's most important waterways for oil exports is located here. The port of Fujairah is an important storage and transshipment location, especially for oil. Tensions in the region have recently increased massively. The background to this is the conflict with Iran. Saudi Arabia and the UAE regard the Islamic Republic as their arch-enemy. The two Saudi tankers were to deliver crude oil to customers in the USA on behalf of the state-owned Saudi Aramco, said Minister Al-Falih according to a report by the state news agency SPA. There were no injuries and no oil was spilled. The ""attack"" was intended to hit the global oil supply. The Arab League and the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC), which is dominated by Saudi Arabia, warned of an escalation of the situation. ""Threats on land or sea borders and on transportation and trade routes against any member of the Arab League are an unacceptable violation of Arab national security."" The Arab League comprises 21 Arab states in the Middle East and Africa as well as the Palestinian territories. The GCC spoke of a ""dangerous development"" and a ""threat to maritime shipping"" in the region. Iran demanded an investigation into the alleged sabotage attempts. Foreign Office spokesman Abbas Mussawi called for a ""complete investigation"" and spoke of negative effects on the security of the Persian Gulf. The USA had recently increased the pressure on the Iranian leadership massively, including with sanctions and military threats. Meanwhile, German Foreign Minister Heiko Maas warned his US counterpart Mike Pompeo against a war with Iran at a meeting in Brussels. The SPD politician said in the conversation on the sidelines of an EU ministerial meeting that he did not want to see a military escalation.

Bosnia and Herzegovina: Parties agree on government formation An important point of contention between the parties was Bosnia and Herzegovina's attitude towards NATO. While the Croatian and Bosnian sides were in favor of joining NATO, the Serbian representation was against it. The government agreement now contains a vague promise to deepen the relationship with the Western defense alliance. The cabinet must now be formed within 30 days. Otherwise the government agreement would lose its validity, said the pro-Russian Serb leader Milorad Dodik (SNSPS) after the meeting. The European Union welcomed the agreement as an ""important step forward"". The formation of a government is also necessary in order to drive forward the country's integration process into the EU. An EU spokeswoman called on the party representatives to ensure functioning institutions without delay. Bosnia and Herzegovina's political system is highly complex. It goes back to the Dayton Peace Agreement, which ended the Bosnian war in the 1990s. It is particularly complicated because the democratic state of Bosnia and Herzegovina is made up of the Muslim and Croatian Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina on the one hand and the Serbian Republika Srpska on the other. Half of the country's 3.5 million inhabitants are Muslims, while around 30 percent are ethnic Serbs. The majority Catholic Croats, who make up 15 percent of the population, feel dominated by the Muslims. Nobody has taken the time here, which is why nothing works. No major project was carried through, at best it was started, then undone again because there was a lack of courage, or people realized that they had been making a mess of things the whole time. Since the state was founded, governments in Bosnia-Herzegovina have achieved virtually nothing. The major parties of the population groups are blocking each other in foreign and domestic policy. Even if they formally form a government. In terms of language, Serbs, Bosniaks and Croats are at most speakers of very close dialects and their religions (Orthodox, Islam, Catholic) differ only in the details. But the hatred resulting from the civil war and mafia structures keep bringing populists to power who work against each other and paralyze the state. ""The formation of a government is also necessary in order to advance the country's integration process into the EU."" The EU has long since exceeded its critical mass. And yet, instead of finally tackling the overdue internal renewal, it continues to burden itself. The British are already out, and now more Balkan states are joining them. They came together under pressure from the EU and the leading Serbian politician is directly threatening not to allow the government to come into being after all (if he doesn't get his preferred candidates through). Since he and his people will have the goals of the other two heads of state, such as rapprochement with the EU and NATO, torpedoed wherever possible, I estimate that the government will implement little or nothing this time either. Without agreement between the representatives in the presidency and the most important representatives of the two federal states, no important reforms will succeed in the state. This was all too rarely the case and will unfortunately remain rare.

Abuse in war Maas and Jolie fight together against sexual violence With a UN Security Council resolution, Federal Foreign Minister Heiko Maas wants to give the global fight against sexual abuse in war more clout. dpa. Prior to the opening of the debate on Tuesday (today), Maas and the US actress Angelina Jolie, UN Special Envoy for Refugees, addressed the public together. Jolie has been campaigning against sexual violence in crisis areas for years and works for the UN refugee organization UNHCR. In a joint guest article for the ""Washington Post"" on Monday, Maas and Jolie described examples of the fates of women in crisis countries. Among other things, they complained that the international community had been unable to prevent the atrocities in Syria and Myanmar. The Congolese doctor and Nobel Peace Prize winner Denis Mukwege, who has treated three generations of raped women and girls from one family in his clinic in Congo, will report on his experiences to the UN Security Council. Jolie and Maas want the perpetrators to be brought to justice. To this end, crimes are to be systematically recorded and investigations facilitated. Victims should also be given more support and their complaints heard. ""Rape and other forms of sexual violence are used as a tactic of war and terror worldwide,"" Maas and Jolie wrote. All too often, perpetrators get away with it. ""This impunity has devastating consequences."" They added: ""We have both met survivors in countries such as Iraq, Bosnia and Sierra Leone who have urged us to address the lack of prosecution that allows sexual violence to continue."" Maas wants to use Germany's current presidency of the UN Security Council to advance the issue. For example, the Security Council is to adopt a resolution that outlines the consequences for supporters of sexual violence against women. Targeted sanctions against perpetrators and their leaders are also being considered. An informal working group is to deal with the issue. Back in 2000, at Namibia's initiative, the Security Council called in Resolution 1325 for women to be protected, included on an equal footing in peace negotiations and reconstruction and prosecuted for criminal offenses. In 2008, Resolution 1820, initiated by the USA, called for more action by states against sexual violence as a method of warfare and brought sexual violence into play as a deciding factor for sanctions. Pramila Patten, the UN Special Representative on Combating Sexual Violence in Conflict, has not seen any significant reduction in the number of cases despite years of efforts by the United Nations. She said in New York that one of the problems was that violence was often caused by non-state actors over whom the UN had no influence.

Complaint to federal states ARD and ZDF allegedly waived funds This week, the collecting society Corint Media (formerly VG Medien) sent a nine-page complaint to the 16 heads of the German state chancelleries. It is about the fact that the public broadcasters do not take care of their ancillary copyrights. According to Corint, they lost tens of millions of euros as a result. However, this is only of secondary importance, because above all ARD and ZDF are distorting the German media market with this negligence and weakening the negotiating positions of German broadcasters and publishers vis-à-vis the digital groups in the long term. This will become important this summer when Germany implements the EU directives on copyright in a legislative package that was approved by the Bundestag last week and will be put to the vote in the Bundesrat on Friday. Corint Media is for private television and radio broadcasters and a number of publishers something like Gema for musicians and composers or VG Bildkunst for photographers and filmmakers. It ensures that royalties are paid and distributed. Corint Managing Director Markus Runde has long been struggling with the problem that ARD and ZDF simply give away a lot of their content and associated rights. ""This gives them a competitive advantage over others in the newly emerging rights licensing markets, which also have to finance themselves by enforcing their copyrights and ancillary copyrights. Why should Facebook and Google pay appropriate remuneration for zeit.de when they can use the press product tagesschau.de for free?"" Especially now that the digital groups have reduced the advertising markets for traditional media to a fraction of their former revenues. ""You can only afford this generous attitude if you are not dependent on such financing options."" Like the public broadcasters, who earn billions every year through license fees. ""At the time, the public broadcasters had seven years to make efforts to obtain their ancillary copyrights"" It still seems a little early to complain about the squandering of a right that has not even come into force yet. Round finds it rather too late. There was already an ancillary copyright for the press. This was issued in August 2013, but withdrawn in 2019 due to legal formal errors. ""The public broadcasters had seven years to enforce their ancillary copyrights, but simply failed to do so and did nothing to secure advantages in the presentation of their content on these large platforms. We want to avoid increasing this distortion of competition to the detriment of private press products and broadcasters on the one hand and license fee payers on the other when the new law comes into effect."" The complaints in the letter, which is available to the Süddeutsche Zeitung, are very detailed. Corint has calculated that the ARD and ZDF radio and television stations have foregone around 4.3 million euros per year. Because this concerns the use of the stations in commercial and public facilities such as hotels, fitness centers, hospitals, retirement and nursing homes, this is still low compared to the license fees that the stations' news portals on the Internet could have demanded for licenses. Corint would generate between 37 and 54 million euros per year for tagesschau.de alone. This waiver is a problem for private-sector media such as RTL, Pro 7, but also Der Spiegel and Süddeutsche Zeitung (which is not a member of Corint Media) primarily because the digital groups could in future be more likely to use content from providers who do not exercise their performance rights. ARD headquarters has not yet received the complaint. Nevertheless, a reaction comes from the WDR headquarters in Cologne. ""Public service broadcasting is subject to different restrictions and requirements than commercial broadcasters and press companies represented by Corint Media,"" it says. ""From ARD's point of view, it is particularly wrong that the state broadcasters could claim the ancillary copyright of the press publisher for themselves. You are not a protected producer of press products. They were therefore not entitled to the ancillary copyright introduced into German copyright law in 2013. We also informed VG Media of this at the time upon request. The same applies to the new European ancillary copyright law, the implementation of which has just been passed by the Bundestag. This is also only granted to press publishers for press publications. At this point in time, we can therefore only take note of the accusations with irritation."" Markus Runde is concerned about the rifts in the German media industry: ""On the user side, there are monolithic blocks like Google and Facebook, tightly organized global corporations that have completely different options. On the rights provider side, there is a fractured field of publishers and other content providers. Content providers will only overcome the asymmetry between publishers, broadcasters and exploiters if they jointly enforce their rights against the exploiters, ideally even at European level.""

Guaidó courts the military: Power struggle in Venezuela: Maduro relies on the military In the power struggle in Venezuela, President Nicolás Maduro has called on the armed forces to be ready to defend themselves against an ""imperialist conspiracy"". In the state of Cojedes, he visited a maneuver on Saturday in which 5,000 soldiers took part. ""A handful of traitors who sell out to the US will not stain the honor of our armed forces,"" Maduro said at the El Pao military base. According to the Colombian television station NTN24, all seven people on board died in the crash of a military helicopter that was accompanying Maduro's flight to the garrison. The cause of the accident was initially unknown. In a failed military uprising on Tuesday, some of those in uniform joined the self-appointed interim president Juan Guaidó. On Friday, the public prosecutor's office issued 18 arrest warrants for military personnel and civilians on charges of treason. No arrest warrant has been issued for Guaidó. Maduro has so far avoided a direct confrontation with his challenger. Guaidó called on the population to march to army barracks and bases in order to persuade the military to change sides. Demonstrators read out a statement by Guaidó in front of the naval command in Caracas and other military units. The military has a decisive role to play in the reconstruction of democracy in Venezuela, according to the appeal to the military, as reported by the newspaper ""El Nacional"". However, the military leadership, which occupies important positions in the economy, has so far stood by Maduro. Russia's Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov is planning talks with his Venezuelan counterpart Jorge Arreaza on the future of the Latin American crisis country. At the meeting in Moscow on Sunday, possible solutions to the power struggle within the framework of the Venezuelan constitution will be discussed, the Russian Foreign Ministry announced on Saturday. The economic situation following the US sanctions against Maduro's leadership was also to be discussed, according to reports. Russia and the USA accuse each other of exacerbating the crisis in Venezuela. Washington supports Guaidó. Russia, for its part, has sent military advisors to Venezuela to support the pro-government armed forces and is backing Maduro. On Friday, Kremlin leader Vladimir Putin and US President Donald Trump spoke on the phone about the escalation in the conflict, among other things. On Monday, Lavrov is due to meet with US Secretary of State Mike Pompeo on the margins of the Arctic Council in Finland. The situation in Venezuela will also be discussed. On Saturday, Pompeo accused Maduro's government of serious misconduct. ""The repression perpetrated by Nicolás Maduro is limitless,"" Pompeo wrote on Twitter. Government forces attacked a Catholic church service, drove into the church on motorcycles, used tear gas and injured many people. ""We stand with the Venezuelan people and with Interim President Juan Guaidó,"" Pompeo wrote.

Terror in Vienna puts Nehammer under pressure Possible omissions by the authorities in the run-up to the Islamist attack in Vienna are putting Interior Minister Karl Nehammer (ÖVP) under increasing pressure. In the National Council session on Thursday, the FPÖ tabled a motion of censure against Nehammer on the occasion of the attack, which was also approved by the SPÖ. The NEOS did not go along ""today"", but threatened to do so next time. A call to resign came from the ranks of the Green coalition partner. Martin Margulies, local councillor and budget spokesman for the Vienna Green Party, vented his anger on Twitter. ""Why is @karlnehammer still in office? He doesn't have his departments under control. A recognizable terrorist attack was not prevented. Four people died. And all this becomes known within 48 hours. What's next?"" Nehammer himself, the Vienna Police Commissioner Gerhard Pürstl and the Director General for Public Security, Franz Ruf, appeared in public again this afternoon and announced new details about the ongoing investigations. According to the report, eight of the 15 suspected Islamists arrested after the terrorist attack in Vienna have already been convicted of various crimes, two of them for an attempted honor killing in Linz. Investigations outside Austria. It was also announced that one line of investigation leads to Switzerland and another to another country. Which country this is was not revealed. At the same time as the press conference in Vienna, however, Interior Minister Horst Seehofer announced from Germany that the Viennese assassin had links to Germany. ""Due to the case in Vienna, we also have links to Germany to dangerous individuals who are monitored around the clock,"" said the CSU politician in the Bundestag on Thursday. Read also: Kurz calls for a new approach to dealing with dangerous people Nehammer, Pürstl and Ruf also had to explain their massive criticism of the authorities, according to which they had failed to prevent the attack. Pürstl rejected these accusations and said that ""we have done a good job"". However, it emerged from his statements that the Federal Office for the Protection of the Constitution and Counterterrorism (BVT) did not take offensive action against the assassin in Slovakia following indications of an attempted purchase of ammunition by him, but only initiated a risk assessment. Sharp criticism from the opposition. In parliament, the three opposition parties gave the Minister of the Interior a good talking to and demanded a complete investigation. The leader of the Freedom Party and former Interior Minister Herbert Kickl (FPÖ) said to his successor: ""What you call a communication error was the death sentence for four innocent people."" The attack could have been prevented if he had known what to do as Interior Minister, Kickl suggested to Nehammer that he should resign. The Social Democrats were not sparing with their criticism either. It is not about obfuscation, distraction and platitudes, it is also about taking personal responsibility, recommended party and club leader Pamela Rendi-Wagner to the ÖVP minister. Now the events must be dealt with honestly and with the courage to admit mistakes. The commission of inquiry announced by Nehammer does not appear to be the appropriate instrument for this, according to Jörg Leichtfried, deputy chairman of the parliamentary group. Parliamentary control is needed, he demanded. Also interesting: Terror in Vienna - What's behind ""Schleich di, du Oaschloch""? NEOS leader Beate Meinl-Reisinger is in favor of the commission, but she wants the opposition to have a say, including in the question of the chairmanship. Overall, it took a much more moderate approach than the SPÖ and FPÖ, although it also disliked Kurz and Nehammer's attacks on the judiciary. She called them ""shabby"". The ÖVP, for its part, pushed for more powers for law enforcement authorities in the pursuit of terrorism. Chancellor Kurz stated that the legal means to monitor and sanction Islamic extremists and other dangerous individuals were not always available at present.

St. Martin: soldier against his will, pacifist by conviction Almost every child knows that St. Martin shares his coat with the poor beggar. It is probably less well known that the Roman soldier did not actually want to be a soldier - but that he was effectively a conscientious objector. ""No one may be forced to do military service with a weapon against their conscience."" The young Martin of Tours would probably also have referred to this sentence from the Basic Law. However, in his time in the Roman Empire, there was of course no constitutional right to conscientious objection as there has been in Germany since 1949. One of the first conscientious objectors? So the future churchman initially followed in his father's footsteps as a Roman soldier, explains Protestant theologian Uwe Metz. Martin's father was a tribune, and according to the custom of the time, it was customary for the son to follow in his father's footsteps. ""But he really only did it against his will - because he was a soldier and he was baptized. And he then made up his mind to say: ""The military and the Christian - that's not compatible, so he actually resigned from the service very early on."" He became a gun refuser - citing the Christian faith: ""Thou shalt not kill. Not the first conscientious objector, but certainly one of the best known. At that time, in late antiquity, Christian pacifism was very widespread, according to the theologian Metz. ""All things military and soldierly were not a matter for the church or the Christian faith, they were left to the rulers."" Reach for the sword to divide the coat. After all, Jesus also called for non-violence and love of enemies. Martin, who later became Bishop of Tours, only took up arms once during his short time as a soldier. And that is what he is best known for today, says Metz. ""The only time St. Martin wielded a sword was when he divided the cloak."" The theologian Metz deduces from this: ""As a true Christian, you can only be a pacifist."" For a long time, the idea of a ""just war"" was the order of the day. However, the churches have not always remained as faithful to their pacifist beginnings as St. Martin. For centuries, the doctrine of ""just war"", which was introduced into the tradition of the Church by the Doctor of the Church, Augustine, a contemporary of St. Martin of all people. Today, both major churches have military bishops who see themselves primarily as pastors for soldiers. Andreas Quirin is a soldier and a Catholic. No contradiction for him. In principle, all people, including soldiers, love peace. ""There is no one who is just waiting with a knife between their teeth to finally be allowed to go to war and then use violence,"" says Quirin. Nevertheless, it is also clear: ""Of course, we are not an armed, technical aid organization that is only sent out to drill wells or build houses."" Being a faithful soldier - no contradiction? And that is the right thing to do in cases where soldiers take up arms. He also has the support of the community of Catholic soldiers, of which Quirin is the chairman. In such cases, the devout soldier does not believe in pacifism without violence or weapons: ""I think that's an absolutely naive idea. The beginnings in Afghanistan have shown that military force is of course needed to put those who are aggressively trying to assert their interests in their place and then to make it possible to provide civilian reconstruction aid."" However, the use of weapons is always the last resort because everyone knows that this would have devastating consequences that nobody wants. St. Martin as a role model for soldiers today. So has St. Martin and his Christian pacifism become obsolete as a role model? Not at all, says Quirin. After all, even soldiers do not act unethically, but rather - like Martin - they must always put their actions to the test before their conscience and God. ""Of course, that's something that should actually be standard for us soldiers in this day and age, that we take a critical view of certain things and question certain things. And in that respect, I think it's a good example that could also apply to us today.""

Venus was probably always a hostile ""hell"" Venus, Earth's sister planet, may never have harbored oceans. This is presumably what new computer simulations suggest. The climate therefore did not allow water vapor to condense there. The new findings contradict earlier estimates that there may once have been oceans on young Venus. By comparison, there have been oceans on Earth for almost four billion years. Experts are divided as to whether liquid water has ever eaten its way into Venus. A team led by astrophysicist Martin Turbet from the University of Geneva has now added another piece to the puzzle in the journal ""Nature"". ""We simulated the climate of Earth and Venus at the very beginning of their evolution, more than four billion years ago, when the surfaces of the planets were still molten,"" Turbet is quoted as saying in a press release from the University of Geneva. At that time, the celestial bodies resembled a gigantic pressure cooker. And according to the researchers, the temperatures on Venus were never low enough for the water vapor in the atmosphere to condense and pour down on the planet in the form of rain. This is because clouds, which preferentially formed on the night side of the planet, created an enormous greenhouse effect that prevented Venus from cooling down sufficiently - and thus the formation of oceans. Several missions to Venus planned Over the next ten years, the European and American space agencies ESA and NASA will send three missions to Venus. And the United Arab Emirates also want to launch a probe in 2028 to orbit the planet and collect data. The observations obtained will be crucial ""to confirm - or refute - our work,"" said Geneva professor and co-author of the study, David Ehrenreich. ""If the authors are correct, Venus has always been a hellhole,"" write US researchers James Kasting and Chester Harman in an article accompanying the study. In fact, Venus today is a ""hellhole"": the thick atmosphere consists mainly of carbon dioxide, the air pressure is incredibly high and temperatures are around 470 degrees Celsius day and night. The astrophysicists also showed in their simulations that the Earth only narrowly avoided the same fate as Venus. If the Earth had orbited the sun just a little more closely or if our central star had shone as brightly as it does today, it would now be just as inhospitable a planet as Venus. Third smallest planet in our solar system Venus - with a diameter of 12,100 kilometers almost as large as our Earth - is the second innermost and third smallest planet in the solar system with an average distance to the sun of 108 million kilometers. Earth's inner neighbor orbits our central star in just under 225 days. However, because the planet rotates very slowly on its own axis, a Venus day is longer than a Venus year at 243 Earth days. The planet is enveloped by a closed, opaque cloud cover, its atmosphere consists mainly of carbon dioxide, with smaller amounts of nitrogen, water vapor and sulfur dioxide as well as traces of gases.
