Tens of thousands of patients a day did not close the schools. Kanievsky's funeral Yes, the Ministries of Education and the Interior easily approved the closing of hundreds of educational institutions across the country due to the rabbi's funeral. The police and the government could have taken many measures to reduce harm to parents and students, but chose the easy way For the past six months, the government has refused to move the schools to distance learning even for one day. Classes in kindergartens and schools continued as usual, even though hundreds of thousands of students were infected in the classrooms, and tens of thousands of teachers could not come to teach due to illness or isolation. The message of the Minister of Education, Yifat Shasha-Biton, was "the easiest thing was to close the education system", and therefore the schools were instructed to remain open no matter what - even when there were no teachers in them and no classes were held in them, and even at the height of the epidemic, while students arrived without tests Corona. This message remains valid despite an epidemic that threatens to collapse the hospitals. However, last night (Saturday), it became clear how easy it is to shut down the studies in the education system throughout Gush Dan and the central settlements - because of Rabbi Kanievsky's planned funeral journey. The Ministry of Education hastened to inform the local authorities about the transition to distance learning, since in any case the teaching staff cannot get to the schools because of the blocking of the roads. As of last night, more than 500 schools and kindergartens have already reported switching to distance learning, and hundreds more of having a partial school day. In addition, for the first time since the first wave of the Corona virus, the Ministry of Education approved the closing of the special education institutions, which have remained open since May 2020. The ministry even approved stopping the transportation system for students in special education. Ayalon Road, Albukar. It turned out that the roads to some of the settlements in the center were actually not blocked - so it was possible to hold studies The funeral procession held in Bnei Brak led to the closing of educational institutions not only within the city, but also in Tel Aviv, Ramat Gan and Givatayim, and also in settlements further away, such as Kfar Saba, Hod Hasharon, Ra'anana, and Kadima-Zoran. Even schools that continued to operate received permission to cancel trips and tests. But in the morning, it became clear that the roads to Tel Aviv and some of the settlements in the center were actually not blocked - so it was possible to hold classes in hundreds of kindergartens and schools, and reduce the harm to students and parents. It seems that the Ministry of Education and the local authorities looked for and found a reason to cancel the studies. It seems that the decision to close the education system in Gush Dan and the surrounding area was made too easily, without appreciating the enormous damage to the students and their parents, and especially to the special education students. It was possible, for example, to postpone the closing of the roads by an hour, to allow the teaching staff to reach the kindergartens and schools, since in any case the funeral was postponed to 12. Another option was to compensate teachers who would have been stuck in the central area after graduation due to the continuation of the blockades, or to give a few hundred of them special permission to come to teach, thus preventing the closure of at least some of the institutions. Alternatively, it would be possible to organize convoys of buses from Jerusalem and the ultra-orthodox settlements in the center of Bnei Brak, in order to reduce congestion and roadblocks. In general, it seems that it was easier for the government ministries and the police to call on hundreds of thousands of students and parents not to come to the educational institutions, workplaces and medical treatments in Gush Dan, than to try and reduce the consequences of the road blocks. By the end of the day, all the students of the center will learn not only who Rabbi Kanievsky was and how important he was to the ultra-orthodox public, but also how easy it is to close their schools.

What are the chances of getting cancer - and what are the chances of recovering from it? A cancer diagnosis was until a few years ago a death sentence, but the field of medicine is developing, and for many types of cancer there are already effective treatments, and even tools that help prevent the disease. On the occasion of Cancer Day, which is celebrated today (Friday), we invited Prof. Ido Wolf, director of the oncology department at the Ichilov Hospital, to the "Expert Clinic" studio, to ask what we must know about cancer today - and what the future holds for us. "Oncology is considered a very tough field, many are not even able to say the words oncology or cancer, the newspaper always says 'severe diseases' or 'complex conditions'," said Prof. Wolff, "but in the end, cancer is another disease, in my opinion Not even the most difficult, there are more difficult things. I'm not sure that terrible dementia is easier than cancer." According to him, the most important thing to know about cancer is that "in recent years there has been a big change in the field of cancer treatment. If it used to be a death sentence, if we look at Israel's statistics, the chance of getting cancer is decreasing, and the chance of recovery is increasing. So the news is good." Prof. Wolff also had an encouraging answer to the question about the price that cancer patients pay during complex treatments such as chemotherapy. "First of all, if we detect it early we will need less treatments," he explained, "and if we do need treatments - even here there are already big changes than there used to be." True, there is still chemotherapy, especially in breast cancer, where this is what causes hair loss and more side effects, but in other cancers we have been able to give much less harsh combinations, and in some cases we switch from chemotherapy treatments to all kinds of biological and immune treatments that are much easier for the patients, so in a sense we have successes". Even in the more difficult cases, Prof. Wolf emphasizes, it is usually a very tough war of several months, "but we do this war to reach 120 later. The advantage of today's treatments is that the vast majority of patients - we can cure them, and 120 is a realistic forecast, to recover from cancer. So it's true, there will be some difficult months along the way, even very difficult, but the optimistic side is that if I have a 35 or 40-year-old patient with breast cancer, who in the past I would have known she would die of this cancer, today I know that after a few difficult months she will be able to live and have The family and the children, and even the grandchildren," he said. One of the problems with cancer, especially the metastatic and simple one, is that it is sometimes difficult to find or locate it, but also in this field there has been significant progress in recent years. "Today there are already blood tests that are developing in this direction, that can detect really tiny elements of the tumor in the blood, super super sensitive tests, that can detect even if there is a minimal disease," said Prof. Wolff, "It is currently in research, and I can assure you in 3- In 5 years we will use these tests routinely, and we will be able to know who has or does not have the small things and adjust treatment better. And more than that, I assume that in 3-5 years we will test healthy people, and already with a blood test we will be able to detect the cancer." More about cancer in Vala! Health: today we are not there yet, there are only regular screening tests that can be done to detect early cancer, "but in a few years, which is not long, each of us will go to the doctor and have a blood test done and look for the cancer at an early stage," explained Prof. Wolff . He added that in England they have just started a study on exactly this test, they plan to test several hundreds of thousands of people, "so a study that is actually being carried out today will produce results in two, three, four years, and it is likely that in not many years each of us will go to the doctor once every few years "Give me a blood test and tell me if I have cancer." He added that "the test already exists, it is in hand, I think that in 10 years our conversation will be completely different. When there is cancer, most people look for a cause, but it is not always possible to find it. "When someone has cancer, they try to find the cause, it's natural, and many times the cause of cancer is attributed to all kinds of events that have happened to us, of all kinds and species." However, according to Prof. Wolff, about 5 percent of cancer cases are the result of genetics and heredity, 30-35 percent are mutations caused by the environment, such as smoking and sun exposure, and about 60 percent are other factors that have no clear cause. "When something happens randomly, the other name is bad luck, and in fact we get a large group of people who say, 'But I behaved well, why did this happen?' And the real answer is that many of the processes are biological processes that behave according to a mathematical model, and they don't exactly care what we did or didn't do," explained Prof. Wolf, "you have to understand that." This understanding, of course, should not harm optimism, since as Prof. Wolf made clear the chance of getting cancer decreases, and the chance of recovery increases, but it is important to be able to deal with this diagnosis, which, despite the optimism, is still scary.

How much will the purchase tax on an apartment cost you this year? Every person who purchases a right to real estate in Israel is required to pay purchase tax. This is actually a tax that that person pays to the state for carrying out the transaction. In some cases, you can get an exemption from paying the tax. At the beginning of each year, the tax authority updates the tax rates for the current year and is doing so now as well. How will this affect you? You'll see right away. For more details about attorney Carmit Shafivar we said that the purchase tax is paid to the state for every real estate transaction. The purchase tax is calculated according to the value of the transaction at rates that are updated once a year. There are different tax rates regarding a residential apartment defined as a single apartment, additional apartments beyond this apartment and rights in real estate that are not intended for residential use such as commerce and agriculture. The calculation of the purchase tax rates is done, among other things, in accordance with the consumer price index for the past year. The practical meaning of updating the height of the stairs in case of an index increase is a reduction in the amount of the purchase tax. In other words, the price from which purchase tax liability starts has gone up. According to the CBS data, this year there was a 5.3% increase in the consumer price index. With the beginning of the year 2023, the tax authority is expected to change the tax rates for this year, and it seems that the increase in the price index is expected to benefit the apartment buyers. The increase in the Tenant-Owned Housing Services Index raises the threshold for exemption from purchase tax for the purchase of a single apartment. This means that buyers will pay less tax. The tax rates for 2023, when purchasing a single apartment, state that no tax will be paid on the portion of the value up to NIS 1,919,294. That is, up to this amount, an exemption from payment of purchase tax will be granted. Last year, the year 2022, the tax brackets determined that no tax would be paid up to the amount of NIS 1,805,545. It was also updated that on the part of the value that exceeds NIS 1,919,294 and up to NIS 2,276,526 - a tax of 3.5% will be paid. In 2022, this tax was paid on the part of the value exceeding NIS 1,805,545 and up to NIS 2,141,605. On the part of the value exceeding 2,276,526 NIS and up to 5,873,149 NIS - a tax of 5% will be paid. In 2022, the amount at this level was NIS 2,141,605 and up to NIS 5,525,070. This year it was determined that on the part of the value exceeding NIS 5,873,149 and up to NIS 19,577,165 - an 8% tax will be paid. In 2022, the amount at this level was NIS 5,525,070 and up to NIS 18,416,900. In addition, on the part of the value exceeding NIS 19,577,165 - a tax of 10% will be paid, in contrast to the year 2022 where the amount was NIS 18,416,900. This means that this is good news for the apartment buyers. This year they will be able to purchase a more expensive apartment and enjoy an exemption or a lower purchase tax. The incoming head of the Mossad: Iran is working to realize the nuclear vision under the cover of international protection The head of the new Mossad, David Barnea, said today (Tuesday) that "Iran is working, even at this very moment, to realize its nuclear vision, under the cover of international protection. Under the auspices of the agreement and without it, with lies and concealments, Iran is in constant progress towards a program to produce weapons of mass destruction." Barnea added at his inauguration ceremony that "our security challenges are very big, and at the top of the list is Iran." Prime Minister Binyamin Netanyahu spoke at the Mossad head exchange ceremony, with the appointment of Barnea as Yossi Cohen's replacement, and claimed that the Iranian nuclear project is an existential threat, the "greatest" for the State of Israel. "Whether to threaten us directly with the destruction of a small and concentrated country with nuclear weapons, or whether to threaten us with tens of thousands of missiles or thousands of missiles backed by a nuclear umbrella. It is a threat that threatens the continuation of the Zionist enterprise, and we must fight this threat endlessly," he emphasized. He congratulated the intelligence agency for its fight against the issue, and made it clear that Israel will continue to fight this as long as necessary. "You are doing it, we talked yesterday about actions that were taken and these actions must continue. I said these things to my friend of 40 years, Joe Biden, and I told him: 'With or without an agreement, we will continue to do everything in our power to thwart Iran's arming itself with nuclear weapons.' Because Iran is different from the other countries that have nuclear weapons today. That's why marriage is not an option." Finally, Netanyahu clarified that Israel will not hesitate to confront the White House on the issue. "If we have to choose, I hope it won't happen, between friction with our great friend the United States and the elimination of the existential threat - the elimination of the existential threat is increasing," Netanyahu said. "This falls first of all on you, on the political leadership of the State of Israel, and on you Dadi - you have to do everything, but everything, to ensure that under no circumstances will Iran arm itself with nuclear weapons." Defense Minister Benny Gantz responded to Netanyahu's words, and even though he expressed agreement with regards to the seriousness of the threat from Tehran, he claimed that he had achieved that dialogue with Washington on the issue should be conducted "in closed rooms". "Iran is a threat to regional stability and world peace. It is a country that creates terrorism and promotes a nuclear program that is dangerous for the State of Israel, and yet, Israel is the most powerful country in the region within a radius of 1,500 km from Jerusalem," Gantz said. "The United States has been and will continue to be Israel's most important ally in maintaining its security and its security superiority in the region. The Biden administration is a true friend of Israel, Israel does not and will never have a better partner than the United States. Even if there are disputes, they will be resolved through direct dialogue in the closed rooms and not through defiant dialogue that may harm Israel's security. Netanyahu attacked the law limiting the priesthood: "Gideon, take down the Vasach"; Saar: "He lives in the movie" The chairman of the opposition MK Benjamin Netanyahu (Likud) today (Monday) at the meeting of the Likud faction attacked the bill to limit the term of the prime minister that was approved by the ministerial committee for legislation, and the bill that prevents a person accused of crimes from forming the government. Netanyahu called the proposals "Iranian and Syrian laws", and accused the coalition leaders of violating the will of the public. The Minister of Justice responded to the comments by saying that Netanyahu "lives in a movie". "They are trying to pass an Iranian law that should actually lead to a situation where those who can win the elections will not win the elections," Netanyahu accused, "but there is a problem with passing an Iranian law because what endangers them is that the will of the public will be expressed. This law is too blatant so they start with a preliminary law - a term limit law that does not exist in any parliamentary democracy. In a democracy, the public decides who will lead it, not an arbitrary law that will transfer power to officials or politicians." "It won't help them. The public cannot be stopped. We will win, we will take all these laws and throw them in the trash, and we will return the will of the people to the people," Netanyahu continued. Justice Minister Gideon Sa'ar responded to the remarks at the beginning of a new Hope faction yeshiva, and welcomed the approval of the law by the Ministerial Committee for Legislation. "I am happy that all the government partners came together yesterday to make an important amendment to term limits," said Sa'ar. "I heard the nonsense of the chairman of the opposition who said that this does not exist in any parliamentary democracy. Netanyahu sent me messengers just a few months ago to form a government and suggested that I enact a term limit law and even agreed to enact it retroactively so that he would only have a few years left to serve. Apparently a few months ago it was democratic and now it has suddenly become undemocratic. Netanyahu is living in a movie, I don't know if in an Iranian movie or a Syrian movie. There is a huge majority of Israelis who support this law. We will pass this law and Netanyahu will not be able to cancel it." The alternate prime minister and foreign minister, Yair Lapid, also addressed the issue at the opening of the Yesh Atid faction yeshiva. "We promised and kept it," said Lapid about promoting the law. "Yesh Atid has been fighting for this law since the day it was established. For this we established a government. To do all the things we promised to the citizens of Israel." "This is not the end of the process, there is another way to do it, but if you want to change the country - this is the way. Form a government, pass a budget, then go and start keeping the promises one by one. We are passing this law together with the Minister of Justice, Gideon Sa'ar, who led a smart and precise move. Working together, in close dialogue. Just as we passed the budget with Minister Lieberman, and we will pass the equalization of the burden with Minister Gantz. There is also an advantage in the complex structure of this government. He forces us to talk. to cooperate with people who are different from us. This is what the Israeli center has always said: let's focus on our common goals, not on what separates and divides," said Lapid.

The outcry of the residents of the south against crime: "We feel powerless and greatly afraid" Hundreds of people will demonstrate this evening (Wednesday) in Be'er Sheva against the crime in the Negev, under the title "The Negev is bleeding: the citizens' protest", and will call for the restoration of security to the region. Eti, whose husband was injured during a robbery at a business in the city about a week ago: "We must wake up the public, go up to give a speech at a demonstration shouting: "A man works and they come and rob him, how can this continue? We feel powerless and have great fear." "There is increasing violence," Etti adds, "this is reflected in the harassment of girls, physical violence, crime, no one, everyone in Be'er Sheva is tired of this situation, everyone is frustrated. There are great suspicions among the residents here, it's a loss of control, it happens everywhere." Yohai Peretz, a member of the committee to save the Negev, explains what the residents hope to achieve with the protest: "We are protesting to provoke the government and the local authorities to allocate budgets for the security of the residents. We demand a change in the punishments." We are tired of being harassed, we are tired of burglaries, and we are tired of no police officers on the streets of Beer Sheva and the Negev at all - it is important not to include the Bedouin sector in these phenomena," Peretz emphasizes, "This demonstration is also for the Bedouin residents of the Negev who suffer from the same criminal gangs. We fight for them too." Rad Abu Elkien, a social activist in the Negev, actually opposes the demonstration: "We also demand security, but we don't need demonstrations and mobilization of extremist organizations. In the Negev we have a common goal to live in coexistence, it will be and will continue to be, it is forbidden to divide between the sectors, and it is forbidden to incite against the Bedouin population, together we will manage to overcome the situation. Together we can make the long-awaited change." The protesters will gather outside the district court in Beer Sheva around 18:00, and from there they will march to the city hall. Among the organizations that will participate in the demonstration will be the committee to save the Negev, My Israel, if you want, and Ragivim. The demonstration comes against the background of the publication of the data on the rampant crime in the southern district, according to which almost a quarter of the violent crimes in the country occur in the south, and last year more investigations were opened in the district than in any other district. Among the latest crime incidents, on Saturday, the police arrested a 15-year-old boy in the Hora settlement, who was in possession of a Glock type pistol and two cartridges with bullets. This, after the police were called to the settlement when they received reports of hearing gunshots, and policemen who caught the boy on the spot searched him. On Friday night, masked unknown persons fired from short range at a Berhat business for a long time without interruption, as part of a conflict between families, which broke out after a large fight involving about 20 people. The police arrested a 30-year-old resident of Rahat on suspicion of the act. In the documentation published on social networks, two men wearing masks are seen outside the car, pulling out weapons and opening fire for about half a minute. In the nearby street, people were seen hanging out at the restaurant when they were frightened and when screams were heard in the background. In the meantime, last Tuesday, 600 South District police officers embarked on a huge operation to eradicate crime, using drones, helicopters, dogs and horsemen, and conducted raids throughout the Negev, during which they seized weapons, drugs and a lot of cash. Nachshon Nagler, commander of the Negev region who took office a few months ago, stated: "You cannot argue with the feelings of the citizens. There was a breach of security in Beer Sheva, my job is to restore security to Beer Sheva and the Negev. This is my mission."

"Like a military operation": The Knesset convenes to discuss the first state budget in 3 years The Knesset plenum will today (Tuesday) discuss the state budget for 2021-2022 towards its final approval, and the coalition is preparing for one of the fateful moments for it. If there is no dramatic change, the Knesset will approve the Budget Law and the Arrangements Law at the end of this coming week, after three years since they were last approved. In doing so, the coalition will provide itself with political stability for the coming months. The discussions opened in the plenary at 9:00 with a speech by the Chairman of the Finance Committee, MK Alex Kushnir, as well as with speeches by the chairmen of the committees that promoted the reforms in the settlement laws. The discussions will last about 33 hours, during which the opposition members from the Likud, the ultra-Orthodox factions and the joint list who are expected to oppose the budget will speak, according to a pre-arranged schedule. On Wednesday at 18:30 the debate will end with speeches by Prime Minister Naftali Bennett, Finance Minister Avigdor Lieberman and opposition leader Benjamin Netanyahu. Finance Minister Avigdor Lieberman said at the opening of the discussions: "We have been waiting for this moment for three and a half years. I especially want to thank the Chairman of the Finance Committee, Alex Kushiner. We pass a budget exactly on the day of the Balfour Declaration, the second of November." The Chairman of the Interior Committee, MK Walid Taha (RAM), said in the discussion that "this is the first time that the Arab society is reflected in such a big way in the budget book." After their speeches, the 120 MKs will begin voting on the thousands of reservations and laws for long hours, until Friday at the latest. For some of them this is the first time they will try to approve a budget, and in the coalition they prepared for it in advance "like a military operation", as they say. The chairman of the coalition, MK Idit Silman, and her deputy, MK Boaz Toporovski, sat and tried to analyze "problematic scenarios" and find immediate solutions for them. "This is the first budget for many members of the Knesset and in general we run a complex coalition," explained Toporovski, "therefore it was necessary to prepare for every scenario." The two prepared for scenarios in which one of the MKs would decide to rebel and vote against the budget, or an MK would be found sick with Corona, as well as the possibility that due to the protracted votes, a reservation from the opposition would be accepted, and the plenum would have to stop the discussions, return to legislative amendments in the committees and bring the law to a repeat vote in the plenum . In order to avoid this, the members of the Knesset of the coalition were instructed to enter the plenum in comfortable clothes, without tablets or laptops and to eat light food beforehand so that they would not fall asleep during the votes that would continue into the night. Silman and Toporovsky recruited "line commanders" - a MK who would be responsible for the row in which he sits in the plenum, and even asked the MKs to postpone the flu vaccination that was given this week in the Knesset in order to avoid a situation of "side effects" after the vaccination that would cause them to be absent. The coalition is trying to maintain cautious optimism, and in recent days Finance Minister Avigdor Lieberman held talks with most of the Knesset members in order to identify problems in advance. "I don't foresee any breakdowns on the way," he said yesterday at the faction meeting. "There is broad agreement in the Knesset, the coalition is very cohesive. There shouldn't be a problem." He added: "I am really excited and for me this is a very important day, also for the State of Israel and the economy." The great ultra-Orthodox rabbis, Rabbi Haim Kanievsky and Rabbi Gershon Edelstein, published a public letter against the current government which they called the "government of malice" whose goal is to "hurt the owner of the pillars of the world". The two rabbis, who mainly represent the Lithuanian ultra-orthodox stream, wrote that the members of the government "conspired against the Torah scholars in any way", and mentioned, among other things, the decree of day dormitories, one-time taxation, the kosher reform and the outline of the reformist Western Wall. According to them, the goal of the government ministers and the representatives of the coalition is to "interfere with the Kollel elders in helping their young children, to impose various taxes to make it difficult for Torah students, to harm the kosher food for all the people living in Zion, and also to recognize classes that are foreign to the Masora Judaism and to displace the rule of Halacha, while blaspheming The holy place is a remnant of our temple." The rabbis state in their letter: "Certainly their plot will not succeed" and "these attempts will only add to and strengthen the learners". In response, Rabbis Kanievsky and Edelstein call on the public to "make Kiddush Hashem, strengthen the Torah, virtues and faith."

Europe is burning: London is hotter than the Sahara desert Authorities across southern Europe are struggling to control huge fires in Spain, Greece, France and Portugal, and the death toll from the extreme heat continues to rise. In Spain, helicopters rained water on the flames at temperatures higher than 40 degrees Celsius in a mountainous area that makes extinguishing efforts difficult. Stunned residents watched the high flames and thick smoke over the Jereta Valley. "Climate change affects everyone," said Miguel Angel Tamio. More than a thousand people have died so far due to the ongoing heat wave in Portugal and Spain. The temperature in areas of Spain reached 45.7 degrees Celsius. The Spanish weather agency has issued heat warnings across the country, including in the north. According to the agency, the heat wave may end today (Monday), but temperatures will still remain "extremely high". In Portugal, about a thousand firefighters are trying to save 13 forest fires in the center and north. The Ministry of Health announced that in the last week 659 people died due to the heat wave, most of them adults. In Greece, 71 fires broke out in 24 hours on Saturday. Fires raged in several areas in central Spain and in the north. William and Alan McCurdy from Britain fled to a local sports center after being forced to flee their home on Saturday due to the fires. "It was very quick...at first we didn't think it was serious. I thought the fire was under control and I was surprised to see that it was approaching us," 68-year-old William told Reuters. In France, fires spread over an area of ​​100,000 dunams in the southwest of the country, and more than 14,000 people were evacuated from their homes. 1,200 firefighters are battling the blazes, authorities said. France issued a red alert, the highest, and called on residents to "be alert". In Italy, smaller fires have been raging for the past few days and the forecast is that degrees will remain above 40 in some areas for the next few days as well. In Britain, temperatures are expected to reach 41 degrees Celsius - an all-time high. The British National Weather Service issued a red warning of "extreme heat" for the first time in history. London today is expected to be one of the hottest places in the world - more than Western Sahara, Jamaica in the Caribbean, Malaga in Spain and Athens in Greece. The hot weather is expected to last until tomorrow before cooling off on Wednesday. The meaning of the red alert is that there will be "a widespread impact on people and infrastructure, with significant changes in workplaces and daily routines". Some of the schools will be closed today or end the school day earlier than usual. Network Rail has warned that people should only travel if "it's absolutely necessary", and some line cancellations have already been announced, as well as restrictions on train speeds. Alongside the Bureau of Meteorology's red warning, the British Ministry of Health issued a level four warning, which means "state of emergency". Health Minister Steve Barclay said that ambulance services will be expanded, and emergency centers will be strengthened. The London Ambulance Service said it had recorded 7,000 calls a day since the heatwave began - compared to an average of 5,500 a day. Beaches across the country were busy over the weekend. Water companies in the south and east of England reported a spike in demand that led to low pressure and disruptions in water supply. Experts urge people to drink plenty of water and draw the curtains so that sunlight does not enter. "In this country we treat a heat wave as a situation where you can play in the sun," said Penny Undersby, director general of the Bureau of Meteorology. "This is not the weather we are talking about today." Chester Zoo is closed to visitors during the heatwave.

Weapons instead of drugs: drug smuggling is expanding, criminals are motivated by money but also by nationalism The wave of illegal drug smuggling into Israel from Lebanon, Jordan and Egypt does not stop and only gets worse, in the absence of a hermetic border, and in view of the vacuum created by the lack of military personnel along the borders, the police recognize the strategic threat and invest effort to thwart the smuggling with the help of the IDF. Although they manage to register significant achievements, this does not deter the Israeli and foreign smugglers from continuing their criminal activities and smuggling drugs and deadly weapons to perpetrators of crime and terrorist elements in Israel, among other things, due to the large financial profit they scoop into their pockets. The assessment among security officials is that today in Israel there are tens of thousands of illegal weapons that are strengthened by perpetrators of crime, in Arab society in particular, that have been stockpiled over the years for the purpose of deterrence until actual use that ends in injury and death. The characteristics of the smuggling that has been thwarted in the last three years are usually a larger amount of weapons and ammunition and less drugs such as cocaine and marijuana, and this is due to the huge profit inherent in selling them in Israel. For example, the 4th and 5th generation Glock pistols, among the most advanced on the market, whose cost is estimated at $2,000, are priced in the Israeli market at about NIS 45,000. An M-16, whose cost is estimated at several thousand dollars, is sold on the Israeli market for 90-110 thousand shekels, and a Kalashnikov rifle for 60 thousand shekels. On the other hand, the demand for the Carlo rifle is decreasing due to the operational need of criminals for a reliable and accurate weapon. In the northern district of the police, and with emphasis on the central unit under the command of the head of the Yamar, Meni Binyamin, together with the district YGAL unit, they are well aware of the smuggling phenomenon for many years and have been dealing with it even before it spread to other districts. For example, until Operation Northern Shield in 2018, in which terrorist tunnels of the terrorist organization Hezbollah into Israel were thwarted, the organization tried to maintain calm in the sector and no large-scale smuggling of ammunition was carried out. However, after the operation, there was a dramatic increase in the number of illegal arms smuggling under the auspices of Hezbollah, both in the quantities and the high quality of the weapons. At the same time, the perforated Israel-Jordan border line is more preferred for illegal drug smugglers. In the past, most of the weapons were diverted to the territories, and accordingly, those who led the smuggling operations from the Israeli side were Palestinians living in the territories, who sold a certain part of the weapons to perpetrators of crime in the Arab society in Israel. But today most of the weapons and ammunition go directly to Israeli Arab criminals, and thus the relationship between the parties has tightened to a level where Israeli Arabs, from the Triangle in the north to the Bedouin diaspora in the south, defeat the smuggling operations and manage the ammunition trade without any fear. The types of goods smuggled at the borders in the district sector change dramatically all the time, from drugs to weapons, and thus, in recent years, the smugglers at the Lebanese border changed phase, and began to prioritize the smuggling of illegal drugs over cocaine and drugs of various types, not only for economic reasons but also for nationalistic reasons. This is the case, for example, in the case of smuggling amlach that was caught while guarding the Walls, including 180 grenades, intended for the "Brothers in the Galilee", that is, for Israeli Arab citizens in the north against police and security forces during the riots at the Walls. Another case, the attack in which Eliyahu Kay was murdered by the terrorist Fadi Abu Shahid in Jerusalem, was carried out using standard weapons that were estimated to have been smuggled from Jordan. The attack that happened at the beginning of the week in the Bekaa against the soldiers' bus was also carried out according to estimates using weapons smuggled from the Jordanian border. On the Syrian border, on the other hand, the weapons smuggling mainly contains Soviet weapons such as Kalashnikovs, while the weapons smuggling on the Jordanian border originating from Iraq mostly contains Western or American weapons. The Jordan-Israel border borders the length of Israel from north to south, and is an interface point between the northern and southern police districts. Since the arrival of the Negev Region Sub-Commissioner Nachshon Nagler, and under the command of Commander Peretz Amr to his position, emphasis has been given to offensive activity against the perpetrators of crime and arms smuggling, this in the face of the increase in the scope of the phenomenon. Since the beginning of 2022, about 12 illegal drug smuggling have been thwarted in the South District, a significant increase from previous years, with five smuggling being thwarted in 2021 and three in 2020. On the Israel-Egypt border, on the other hand, drugs are mainly smuggled, from cannabis of all kinds to cocaine and heroin, which make their way from Ethiopia through Cairo to the Israel-Egypt border, straight to the Israeli drug dealers who are not content with smuggling through flights and mail. Some of the drug smuggling moves in the opposite way, from Israel to Egypt. These are mainly high-quality cloned cannabis seeds that are smuggled into Israel from Europe, mainly from the Netherlands and Belgium, thanks to the good relations between the Israeli and European merchants. From there they make their way to Sinai, where they grow in the fields of Bedouins, who bring back the harvest later on. Drug smuggling at the Egyptian border is in the hundreds every year, but is decreasing as a result of police activity with the help of the IDF.

"If bank employees get an exemption from fees - it's not bad if we reduce them for everyone" The Knesset's Economic Committee approved for first reading the bill that would limit to NIS 360 the commission that a bank may charge for opening a mortgage file. The bill is supported in principle by the Ministry of Finance and the Ministry of Justice. These only object to setting the amount of the ceiling in legislation, and prefer to entrust the flexibility in setting it to the regulator (the Bank of Israel). The current price list allows banks to charge a portfolio opening fee of 0.25% of the loan amount. It turns out that the fee for opening a case currently ranges between NIS 820 and 5,800, depending on the amount of the mortgage. Apparently, regardless of the bank's operational costs - which every commission is required to cover. "In 2021, the public took out 130,000 mortgages totaling 116 billion shekels, which allowed the banks to collect a commission of 0.25% - and collect 290 million shekels. The banks need to make a profit, but they take more because they can, while the public is held captive. It's pigs for its own sake," MK Haim Katz (Likud), who initiated the bill with MK Eti Atia, said at the hearing. "Not everyone pays the commission," added Katz. "There are strong people who get a discount, and there are weak people who don't get it, because no one counts them." Bank of Israel data show that the percentage of discount recipients increased in the last two years from 61% to 73%. Most of them received discounts of 60%-80%, and about 15% received a full 100% discount. However, even last year, 27% of mortgage borrowers did not receive a commission discount at all. MK Shlomo Karai (Likud), asked the representative of the Bank of Israel if the regulator knew the identity of the recipients of the full exemption. When she answered in the negative, he said: "Let me tell you. These are mainly the tens of thousands of bank employees and their families, who enjoy a full exemption - and if these tens of thousands receive a 100% discount, the banks can probably manage even without such a high commission." According to Karai, the Bank of Israel's data regarding the rate of discount recipients is distorted, because sometimes the banks condition the acceptance of the discount on the customer's consent to additional services (for example, opening a bank account). Karai also pointed out that collecting the commission as a percentage of the loan amount is a distortion that is repeated even when collecting a bank guarantee fee that is backed by a deposit. "The bank doesn't have a job there. He simply freezes my money, which is lying with him - and charges me a kind of interest, because instead of paying a fixed fee - I pay an annual percentage on the deposit." The Bank of Israel prefers to postpone the legislation after the reform of the mortgage market is completed (this August). The institution claims that the fee for opening a case is accepted in the world, and that the maximum rates in Israel are lower than those used in the world. However, those in favor of the law claim that there is no reason to charge a fee as a percentage of the loan - since this is intended to cover fixed overheads. "If the yield on 30-year government bonds is negative - the banks make enough money on mortgage interest, and there is no reason for a mortgage handling fee to be derived as a percentage of the amount of the loan," Katz added.

In the background of the attempt to promote normalization with Israel: Biden's senior advisers secretly arrived in Saudi Arabia Two of the senior advisers of the President of the United States, Joe Biden, made a secret visit to Saudi Arabia for talks on the mediation between Israel and Saudi Arabia, which was revealed in Walla! this week Other topics that will come up for discussion are the American demand for increased oil production as well as the preparations for Biden's planned visit to the Kingdom at the end of June - according to three American sources. President Biden plans to visit Saudi Arabia as part of his visit to the Middle East which will also include Israel and the Palestinian Authority. In order for the visit to take place, the parties need to finish formulating a package of understandings on these issues between the US and Saudi Arabia. According to three American sources, President Biden's senior adviser on the Middle East issue, Brett McGurk, and the American energy envoy Amos Hochstein, who is considered very close to Biden, arrived in Saudi Arabia on Tuesday to hold meetings with Saudi officials. At the White House they refused to comment. The US State Department said: "We have nothing to disclose about travel at this stage." On Monday night it was published in Walla! Because the Biden administration is secretly mediating between Israel, Saudi Arabia and Egypt in an attempt to achieve a series that will complete the transfer of the islands of Tiran and Fin in the Red Sea to Saudi sovereignty, and that will include a separate course of Saudi normalization measures towards Israel. If the negotiation ends successfully, it may pave the way for significant normalization steps on the part of Saudi Arabia towards Israel. Such a development would be a significant breakthrough and a major political achievement for the Bennet-Lapid government and the Biden administration in the Middle East. The White House wants to reach an understanding on the issue before Biden's planned trip to the Middle East at the end of June. The Saudi Foreign Minister, Prince Faisal bin Farhan, was asked about the publication in Walla! during a panel at a conference in Davos on Tuesday. He did not deny the existence of the negotiations. "We have always said that normalization is the end result of a path that needs to be taken," said the Saudi Foreign Minister. "Normalization between the region and Israel will be beneficial, but we will not be able to reap all these fruits if we do not address the Palestinian issue. The fact that this issue is not resolved creates instability in the region. The first priority should be to achieve progress in the Israeli-Palestinian peace process and if this happens it will benefit the entire region." President Yitzhak Herzog said during a panel at the Davos conference that Saudi Arabia is an important country and Israel would like the Saudis to join the Abraham Accords. "It's a process and it takes time," Herzog said. Biden wants the Saudis to increase oil production. So far, despite several requests, the Saudis refuse and claim that the oil market is balanced and there is no need to inject more oil into the market. The reason why Biden needs the Saudis to increase oil production is to try to lower the price of fuel in the world and especially in the US, in preparation for the mid-term congressional elections in November. Increasing oil production is also important to Biden against the background of the war in Ukraine and the sanctions he wants to impose on Russian oil. Without additional Saudi oil on the market, Biden will find it difficult to advance such sanctions. The Saudis have emphasized so far that they will not violate an agreement they signed with Russia on setting oil production quotas, but this agreement is about to expire in September. This may pave the way for a Saudi-American agreement to be implemented in the future, but announcing it will bring down prices and help the American president. If the talks of Biden's advisers in Saudi Arabia on oil, normalization with Israel and other issues are concluded successfully, this will increase the trust between the US and the Saudis and pave the way for Biden's visit. In such a visit, the American president is expected to meet in one way or another with Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman. American intelligence determined that bin Salman ordered the murder of Washington Post commentator Jamal Khashoggi. Against this background, Biden called Saudi Arabia during his campaign for the presidency a "rebellious country" and promised to take a tough line towards it. A visit by Biden to Saudi Arabia may symbolize a significant change in this American policy.

Precedent PSAD: A controlling owner can purchase the shares of the public company under his control at the market price only When a controlling owner purchases the shares of the public company under his control, two major problems arise: the conflict of interest and the price. This week, the judge of the Central District Court, Benny Arnon, dismissed a derivative suit against the controlling owner and officers of the Optibase real estate company. Arnon, in a comprehensive 130-page ruling, ruled in favor of the company regarding three private allocations it made to its controlling owner, Shlomo Weiler, in 2008, 2011 and 2013. According to the plaintiffs, the shareholders Simcha and Baruria Shiloni, the allocations were made with a conflict of interest of the controlling owner who was on both sides of the transaction, and at prices lower than the fair and proper value of the stock on each of these dates. The price question is the central message in the story. In situations where the controlling owner wishes to purchase its shares in order to disappear from the stock market and turn a public company into a private one, strict conditions have been imposed on the board, due to the fear of improper manipulation. For example, if the controlling owner knows about an imminent exit and therefore has an interest in keeping the public away from the expected profits. Therefore, in the case of 'going private' (turning a company from public to private), the controlling owner is obliged to make a "full tender offer" and the price will be determined according to the DCF method - future cash flow - which embodies the future valuation of the company. Arnon stated in the current case that in the absence of suspicion of manipulation, the price will be the market value of the share only. This, after he was convinced of the legitimacy of the reasons for the allocation - the company's need for cash, by way of selling shares to the controlling owner who pours money into it in exchange for shares. "Different from a full tender offer," Arnon wrote, "a private share allocation makes it possible to examine the stock's behavior in the market after the shares are allocated, and accordingly to identify whether the allocation was made at a price that does not reflect the fair value of the share, including due to the use of insider information or due to the choice of timing manipulative to make the allocation by the controlling owner". That is, if the controlling owner Weiler will later profit from the shares he purchased in the allotment, the rest of the stockholders will also profit as well. So it's debatable whether Weiler acted to save the company or took advantage of a business opportunity. But, even if he survives, all shareholders will benefit - unlike in the case where the company was delisted. The plaintiffs claimed that the company did not examine alternative ways of raising funds, such as loans for example or issuing shares to the public. In this matter, the judge ruled in favor of the company, when he applied the 'business judgment' rule. In dealing with the claim of conflict of interest raised by the plaintiffs, Arnon stated that the decision passed the triple approval required for transactions involving interested parties - the approval of the audit committee, the board of directors and the general meeting, with a large majority of untainted shareholders. So the judge applied the essentially procedural rule, which immunizes the officers from lawsuits if they acted in good faith, in the absence of a conflict of interest and in an informed manner, that is, they reviewed and considered the deal. The plaintiffs argued that the stricter test should be applied because it is a transaction in which the controlling owner stands on both sides. This is the "rule of complete fairness" test, which was applied by Judge Dania Keret Meir in the Makhteshim Agan deal. A rule that checks the fairness of the transaction itself, and not just its procedural cleanliness, as required by the "business judgment rule" test. Arnon rejected the demand to apply the strict rule. In his opinion, it should be applied "only when the transaction shows suspicious signs such as a noticeable inequality between the controlling owner and the other shareholders". Arnon stated that "the decision to raise capital for the company was a reasonable and logical decision under the circumstances." The bottom line, summarizes attorney Sharon Lubetzky Hess of Amit Polk Matlon, who represented some of the officers, is that "in the absence of fear of manipulation of the share price, a public company can make a private allocation to its controlling owner at the market price, without being required to carry out a valuation of its shares . In this way, the verdict contributes to creating certainty, which did not exist until now, regarding the proper pricing of the company's shares for the purpose of carrying out a private allocation, which as a rule is a faster and cheaper option for raising capital for the company, certainly in relation to the issue of shares to the public, which requires the publication of a prospectus and additional costs on the side. The controlling owners of the company, Shlomo Weiler and the Capri family, were represented by attorney Shai Tsadik from the office of Fisher Bacher Chen Wall Orion & Co.; the directors, members of the audit committee and the officers of the company were represented by attorneys Sharon Lubetzky Hess and Shahar Haron from the office of Amit Polk Matlon & Co.; The company was represented by attorney Michael Ginzburg and Matan Winkler from Gross Kleinhandler Hodak HaLevi Greenberg & Co. The plaintiffs were represented by attorney Shay Ganor from the office of A.S. Shimron, Malcho Perski and Co.

Bar Siman Tov moves into business: in talks with Discount Capital to establish a fund in the health sector Barsi's new career? The former CEO of the Ministry of Health, Moshe Bar Siman Tov, has recently been in talks with Discount Capital, the investment arm of Discount Bank, to establish a joint investment platform in the field of health technology. This was learned by Calcalist. The relationship between Bar Siman Tov and Discount is handled by Hila Himi-Alpert, CEO of Discount Capital. The talks have been going on for several weeks, but no decision has yet been made on the matter. The goal of both parties is to choose companies for investment in which it will be possible to introduce real strategic value in breaking into international markets. Officially Bar Siman Tov cannot yet be a partner in such a venture due to the cooling off period he is in as is customary after retiring from a senior position in the civil service. The cooling off period is expected to end in May 2021, but this January he will be able to conduct official talks. One of the options being considered is to establish an investment fund as is customary in the field. Sources in Bar Siman Tov's environment said that naturally he is exploring various professional options, including establishing an investment platform in the health sector. The field of health investments has been booming in recent years and is gaining momentum following the establishment of many startups that develop technology in the fields of medical devices, digital medicine and artificial intelligence. About two months ago, the retiring CEO received from Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu an offer to return to a senior position as part of the fight against Corona, but he turned it down. The proposal from Netanyahu came against the background of the murky relations that prevailed between the previous corona projector Prof. Roni Gamzo and Netanyahu, while Netanyahu's relations with Bar Siman Tov in the first wave were considered very good. Since he retired, Bar Siman Tov has continued to express his opinion about the Corona crisis. For example, last September he tweeted that "Israel is at a critical point in time today and I feel that too many people think there is no real danger. And that is important to talk about. The main thing is a safe corona routine. This is what happens in countries that manage to keep morbidity low and here we are less good. We quickly and with great force brought back the studies and events. Today we understand that it was a mistake and are making amends." In an interview with Yedioth Ahronoth a few days ago, Bar Siman Tov said: "There are signs that herald a third wave. You have to think about how to keep the morbidity at a controlled level as much as possible. The vector was and remains education. Students in all settings should study in capsules, and they should be separate from each other. Keeping a large capsule in the morning and mixing it in the afternoon is as if we did nothing. Is closure realistic? Definitely. There are significant factors for morbidity: studies and gatherings. This matter needs to be taken care of now." Bar Siman Tov recently joined the Institute for National Security Studies (INSS) as a visiting researcher under the leadership of Colonel (Ret.) Amos Yadlin, where he is expected to lead the study of the place of the health system in Israel's national security concept, and to conduct studies and policy documents, in collaboration with senior researchers at INSS which will be presented within the framework of the institute and submitted to the public and the decision makers. Discount Capital is an anchor investor in several funds, including Fimi, Vertex, Comra and more. Discount Capital is also invested in Marius Nacht's Amoon health fund. This year, Discount Capital made several investments in companies in the food sector, in the satellite company Image (ISI) and in several technology companies.

MK Toma-Sliaman: "The support of the joint list is conditional on renouncing the deal of the century" The Joint List faction will meet today (Sunday) at noon in Kfar Qassem, to discuss the question of whether to recommend Blue and White Chairman Benny Gantz to the President for the mandate to form the government, as well as to discuss what conditions the list will present in exchange for such a recommendation. It is estimated that if they reach an agreement on the issue, 12 MKs from the Hadash, Ra'am and Tal parties are expected to support the recommendation, while three members of the Knesset from Balad will not support it. Later in the day, MK Aida Toma Sliaman was interviewed on behalf of the List on Aral Segal's program on 103FM, during which she stated that the List's support for granting the mandate to form the government to Gantz is conditional on canceling the deal of the century. "If Gantz wants us, he should contact us officially after his attitude towards us in the elections. There will be no divide and rule, whoever wants us has to talk to all 15. Those who want us should give up the deal of the century, unilateral annexation and the nationality law." Yesterday Toma-Sleiman addressed the issue of support for the candidates for the government, in response to the statement that Gantz gave yesterday in the village of Maccabiah, and said that "now it is clear, Gantz does not understand that he has no recommendation as long as he does not turn to the joint list directly and publicly. Gantz turn away." Ahead of the faction meeting, Balad chairman Matans Shahada said this morning that the joint list "will not repeat the mistake of recommending Gantz" in talks to form the government. The joint list will not recommend Gantz without clear commitments. We will not make decisions based on insinuations, we learned from last time." He also added that "the Arab parties realized that they could demand, especially when no bloc has 61 mandates, and after, according to the reports, Netanyahu offered them benefits in exchange for not supporting Gantz." MK Shahada later presented his list of conditions for supporting "Blue and White" and said that among the requested conditions his party would demand the repeal of the Kaminitz Law and the Nationality Law as threshold conditions. He concluded his words by saying that "all members of the list will make a decision together." His faction member, MK Sami Abu Shahada, said last night in response to statements made by Netanyahu and Gantz that "Ganz knows what he must do to form a government. We prevented the instigator from Balfour from obtaining a majority in the Knesset, and we will continue to do everything to block his path to the prime minister's chair. The Arab public has put its faith in the joint venture, and we will work to advance its interests and fight for justice, equality, and peace." MK Mansor Abbas, chairman of the National Assembly, also referred to the possibility of supporting Blue and White today and said: "We in the National Assembly sat down yesterday and said that at the moment there is no infrastructure to make a decision to support, recommend or not. There is nothing in our hands that can tell us to go for it. I don't rule out support outright, but there is currently no infrastructure for it. In contact with Blue and White, because of the insult to the honor of the Arabs. I cannot return to the Arab public and say that I have a mandate to recommend him." He later referred to his party's position and said that "BLD has a clear position, it is against recommendation and any kind of participation in support in one way or another. It does not depend on blue and white. This is BLD's position.

Getting started: the deluge of bills has already begun With a delay of two weeks, the 23rd Knesset started this week. Tomorrow (Wednesday) the Knesset committees will be established, and in a coalition they will start enacting the Norwegian law in favor of Blue and White. But the real sign of the start of activity in the Knesset were the many legal declarations that were released into the air. These are not bills that have even the slightest chance of passing through full legislation, but statements of law that are mainly intended for a headline in a newspaper. First it was MK Yulia Malinovski from 'Israel Beytinu' who suggested that the president of the country could not be the one against whom an indictment was filed. The intention is clear: in Israel Beytinu refers to the interpretations according to which Netanyahu is facing the president's residence, and they, for their part, are trying to stop him, if only they had a majority. For now this is a statement of intent. They then did it 'to the right' of their new seats in the opposition. This time they announced the submission of the "French Law" proposal. In this incarnation, Yamina is seeking to prevent the opening of an investigation against a sitting prime minister, but of course the law will no longer apply retroactively to Netanyahu. MK Shaked even said this morning (Tuesday) on the IDF airwaves that she would like to pass this law together with the allocation of the prime minister's term for two terms. This time too, the bill has no chance of progressing on the legislative level, but at least there is a title here and an opportunity to attack the Likud from the outside. Law declarations are a flourishing branch of the Israeli parliament. Members of the Knesset propose thousands of bills every year, but in practice - only a few will enter the hall of fame, that is, the law book of the State of Israel. This time it will be difficult for the opposition and even the coalition to promote legislation, because according to the Blue and White and Likud agreements, no legislation will be promoted in the next six months that is not related to Corona or the budget. The opposition will be required to reduce its tools, and its possibility to act will remain mainly through the committees in the coming months. In order to enable the start of the work of the Knesset, the coalition, led by MK Miki Zohar, reached agreements with the opposition. As part of the agreements, the committee for state audit, the committee for dealing with violence in the Arab sector, the committee for promoting the status of women, as well as another committee will be transferred to the opposition. At the same time, the Likud finished splitting up their committees: the aliyah committee will be in the hands of MK David Bitan and the gas handling committee will be handed over to MK Avi Dichter. The Labor and Welfare Committee will also be in the hands of the Likud and will be headed by MK Haim Katz, and the Corona Committee will be headed by MK Yifat Shasha Biton. The 'Blue and White' committees will be the interior, education and child rights committees. The ultra-Orthodox will receive the economy, constitution, finance and public inquiries committees. Today (Tuesday) members of 'Yimina' tried to reach agreements with Zohar and Knesset Speaker Yariv Levin and take over the State Audit Committee. According to practice, the committee is supposed to be in the hands of the opposition and 'Yimina' proposed MK Ofir Sofer to run the committee with the support of the coalition, instead of Yesh Atid candidate Ofer Shelah. Zohar and Levin refused Yumina's proposal, in order to allow the continuation of work in agreement with the opposition as was customary in the past and especially for the busy day in the Knesset tomorrow (Wed). 'Yimina' is expected to receive, together with 'Israel Beitenu', one committee in a half-term, out of the four committees of the opposition.

The judge in the Netanyahu cases responded to a postponement request: "At the moment there is no change in the dates" The third hearing in the thousands of cases was held today (Sunday) at the Jerusalem District Court. It was a reminder discussion for an update regarding the status of the investigation materials and determining the continuation of the discussions. In his first appearance as Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's defense attorney in Case 4000, Attorney Baez Ben Zur had an argument with the head of the panel of judges, Rivka Friedman-Feldman, and claimed that essential materials were not received in time. Towards the end of the hearing, to which the defendants themselves - Netanyahu, Shaul and Iris Elovich and Noni Mozes - were not required to appear - Attorney Ben Tzur asked to postpone the answer to the indictment that should be given on November 29 until a decision is made on the request concerning the investigation materials as well as the request to amend the indictment. Friedman-Feldman rejected the words: "Currently there are fixed deadlines. As much as it is necessary to change... As of this moment, nothing changes." At the beginning of the hearing, the head of the panel referred to the request of Netanyahu's defense attorneys to hold the hearing on the requests to remove the privilege of the evidence materials before another judge. "In every case where there is a petition to lift privilege, a hearing is held as one party, your request was to transfer the case to another judge, what is different?" the judge asked, and it was agreed that the request would remain for the consideration of the court. Ben Tzur referred to Netanyahu's requests to remove the secrecy and claimed that the request "focuses on the key witnesses, especially the state witnesses in the key operations. We are talking about a procedure that involves three cases, on the face of it it is a complex case, there are precedent issues, media relations and public figures, actions of speakers, it is understandable that there are quite a few lines of defense that should be deployed before the court, hence the complexity of the procedure." Ben Tzur brought as an example of materials that were missing for the defense a document containing a transcript of conversations between state witness Shlomo Filber and journalists, which was only handed over to the defense last Thursday. Of these, it seems that the one who was the CEO of the Ministry of Communications expresses doubt about the strength of the evidence. Filber said, according to the document: "On Friday I got up and saw the headlines, I saw that they were trying to give artificial life to this nonsense of Elovitch and Netanyahu... They invented a bribe here, which is a scarecrow bribe... Noni's bribe is nice for their headlines. It is an apparent bribe. I don't know how to tell you. What we are seeing now is a supreme effort of a system that has been working for two years and has stretched itself to the limit... The police collect pieces of the puzzle, as many pieces as possible, and then decide how to play with the picture of the puzzle. If there's a part that doesn't fit, she removes it." Attorney Ben Zur wondered: "The accuser said that we decided to classify the conversations as relevant, from the beginning we thought they were irrelevant. This is material that until two days ago we did not have at our disposal." Judge Friedman-Feldman: "What do you mean by this, sir? We will not discuss what is not in front of us"? Ben Tzur: "It affects this given discussion... That is why we note the issue, and that they take into account the statements of the accuser that everything was handed over. What arrived on Thursday has weight." Friedman-Feldman: "Sir, with all the general claims, I don't expect us to check all the materials. There is a presumption of normalcy in the conduct of the state, mistakes can happen, regarding the submitted documents we will check them. It is possible to move forward and address and respond specifically to the things requested of the state's claims."

Claim: Juniors took care of the mother, the baby was born injured Parents of a child with cerebral palsy claim that negligence at birth caused the severe damage. According to them, the fetus suffered from disturbances in the oxygen supply but the caesarean section was delayed. A medical malpractice claim against general health services was recently submitted to the Central District Court by parents claiming medical malpractice at the birth at the Meir Hospital which caused the baby severe neurological damage. Through the Gutman-Amir law firm, the parents claim that in May 2016, the mother came to the hospital when she was 38 weeks pregnant, due to suspected water loss, bloody discharge and irregular contractions. Upon arrival, she reported that she could feel the fetal movements very well. According to them, after receiving her, the mother was not given a medical or obstetric examination, nor an ultrasound examination to assess the condition of the fetus. She was connected to a monitor that was pathological and characterized by repeated arrhythmias. The plaintiffs stated that this kind of pathological monitoring required an immediate evaluation by a senior physician and, following that, a decision for an urgent caesarean section. This, especially in view of the advanced week of delivery and the fact that the plaintiff was far from giving birth. Despite this, the attending physician was not called, no assessment of the condition of the fetus was performed, and no intrauterine resuscitation was performed. The prosecutors added that the first monitoring lasted 56 minutes (36 minutes more than necessary) and at the end the specialist who treated her, who was allowed to practice medicine only three months earlier, did not understand the pathological pattern and its severity. Later, the mother was connected to the monitor again and the result continued to indicate severe fetal distress. About six minutes after the start of the second monitoring, an older intern realized the need and urgency of performing a caesarean section and preparations for the operation were even started. Despite this, the surgery itself was performed only about 45 minutes later. Only at this stage did the junior interns - who managed the case alone - inform the duty manager and the senior physician in charge. The doctor ordered a caesarean section, a decision that was made too late. Even after the decision was made, it was claimed, the staff wasted additional valuable time and connected the mother to an unnecessary third monitor. The parents emphasized that due to the significant and negligent delay in making the decision to perform a caesarean section, and in performing the operation itself, the baby was born without a pulse and needed resuscitation. They attached an expert's opinion according to which the management of the birth and the treatment of the monitors deviated significantly from the recommendations of the position paper that was in effect at the time and from the accepted practice in delivery rooms. Another opinion on their behalf stated that the claimant was born suffering from perinatal asphyxia (a disruption in the supply of oxygen to the fetus around birth) and that there is a clear causal link between the asphyxia and his neurological damage. The plaintiffs stated that today their son suffers from severe neurological and developmental damage due to asphyxiation at birth: developmental delay, unbalanced epilepsy and cerebral palsy. According to them, performing a caesarean section at an earlier stage would have resulted in the rescue of their son from the womb in time, and could have prevented his severe damage. The plaintiffs described in the statement of claim the great suffering they and their son are going through, who will depend for the rest of his life on the supervision of others and their help in all daily activities. They stated that their lives have changed completely and they are now focused on their son and his needs. The Meir Hospital responded: "The hospital is unable to provide an answer since the claim has not yet reached it. When the lawsuit arrives, it will be examined with the required professionalism."

Senior American: Iran presents excessive and unrealistic demands in the nuclear talks A senior official approved the publication in Walla! According to which the Iranians demand that the US remove more sanctions than stipulated in the agreement, but are not willing to limit their nuclear program accordingly. According to him, the Biden administration believes that understandings can be reached before the Iranian presidential elections in June, but emphasized that they are also preparing for an explosion in the talks. A senior official at the US State Department, who is participating in the nuclear talks in Vienna, confirmed the publication today (Thursday) in Walla! According to which there are large gaps with Iran in the negotiations, and that the Iranians present excessive demands and are not willing to take the full steps they need to limit their nuclear program. Tomorrow there will be another round of indirect negotiations in Vienna between representatives of the United States and representatives of Iran mediated by the European Union and with the participation of the other powers - France, Germany, Great Britain, Russia and China. So far the negotiations are faltering and there has been no breakthrough. The American official confirmed that the Iranians demand that the US remove more sanctions than stipulated in the nuclear agreement, and that they impose fewer restrictions on the nuclear program than stipulated in the agreement - for example in regards to the advanced centrifuges. "The choice is clear. If they want to return to the nuclear agreement, it is clear what Iran has to do," said the official. "We don't know if the Iranians want to do this or not. It is possible to reach an understanding on returning to the agreement, but it is a matter of a political decision by the Iranian leadership." According to the American official, the Iranians are making excessive demands. However, the American official noted that the Biden administration believes that it is possible to reach an understanding on returning to the nuclear agreement before the Iranian presidential elections on June 18, if the regime in Tehran takes realistic positions during the negotiations, something that has not happened so far. "We think an agreement can be reached," he said. "We are not reinventing the wheel and this is not rocket engineering." In the same breath, the senior official at the US State Department noted that the Biden administration was preparing for a scenario in which Iran would not be ready to fully implement the nuclear agreement and the negotiations would explode. "If this happens, the Biden administration will fight and do everything to make sure that Iran does not have a nuclear weapon - we are also preparing for such a scenario - but we prefer to reach an understanding on returning to the agreement," he said. The American official added that the United States is ready to remove all sanctions that constitute a violation of the nuclear agreement, but demands that Iran return to implementing the agreement as it is worded and in full. "You just have to read the agreement and implement it," said the American official. "There will be no situation for the United States to do more than it needs and Iran to do less. We will see if the next round of negotiations will move things forward or if Iran will continue to make unrealistic demands. There are gaps, but they can be closed if Iran takes a realistic approach."

The appeal was rejected, the members of the Hebrew community are required to leave within 14 days The Population and Immigration Authority rejected the appeal of 51 members of the Jewish community from Dimona who received a deportation order from the country last April. The authority ordered the members of the community to leave the country within 14 days. The letters say they were issued on August 9, but they arrived at the recipients on Monday this week, the eve of the holiday. The members of the community are expected to petition the court in Beer Sheva against the decision in the coming days. Dozens of members of the Jewish community received the deportation orders after in 2015 they applied on their own initiative to the Population Authority with a request to regularize their status, since they had settled in the country without a permit. The community was asked to provide the authority with a list of members without status, and did so. After that, the authority began to contact those without status and demand that they leave the country. Those targeted for deportation submitted appeal requests, and according to the Population Authority, each such case is examined on its merits, but in fact all appeals were rejected. Now they intend to start legal proceedings against their deportation. Attorney Omri Barbash, who represents the members of the Hebrew community together with Attorney Avigdor Feldman, said that they will appeal the decision to the court. One of the rejection letters sent by the Population Authority reached Israel and it details the reasons for rejecting the application of A, a 22-year-old young man from the community who has lived in Israel for the past decade. According to the Ministry of Interior data, A entered Israel in 2011 when he was only 12 years old using a tourist visa. In the letter it was not stated whether A arrived alone or together with his family since the expiration of his license, he is staying in Israel illegally and is doing justice to himself," it was written. Later in the letter it is stated that even if the center of A's life is in Israel, this does not justify receiving status in Israel. Compared to A who came to Israel in the last decade, there are members of the community destined for deportation who were born here. In April, Haaretz brought the story of Little Heraklis, 22 years old, who was born in Israel to parents who arrived in 1998 but never received status. Yilit's mother, Don, received a deportation order in April that also applies to her eight children who live in Israel. "When we received the letter, it created a feeling of despair in me," Herklis said in April. "I was born here, I grew up here, I was educated here, I don't know any other place in the world. This is my home, so why should I leave?" . The Population Authority clarified in April that the deportation was done at the discretion of the then Minister of the Interior, Aryeh Deri. The mayor of Dimona, Benny Biton, then turned to Derai with a request to avoid the deportation of the Hebrews, whom he defined as an integral part of the city. "It is impossible for them to be forced to leave their place of residence and part of their birthplace after many years," he wrote. "As someone who has accompanied the community for many years, I will not let this move happen." MK Mossi Raz (Meretz) today (Saturday) defined the decision as "disgraceful" and said that community members are equal partners in Israeli society. "This is their community and this is their place. This deportation can and should be stopped," Raz said.
