Cashless Nearly 90 percent of Belgians prefer to pay digitally. Even so, 63 percent of purchases in retail stores in our country are still paid with cash, a survey by the banking federation Febelfin reveals. So there is strong consumer demand for cashless payments, but supply is not following. In a lot of larger commercial establishments - clothing boutiques, shoe stores, restaurants, gas stations - paying by card is commonplace, especially if they are chains. But quite a few (retail) merchants - think butchers, bakers, sandwich stores, French fry stores, who usually deal with smaller amounts - only accept cash. They don't install a payment terminal and screen on the grounds that it's too heavy an investment and that they would have to remit a percent per transaction, which further erodes their limited profit margin. That argument is becoming less and less valid. The cost to merchants of electronic payments has fallen. And they forget that cash payments also have fees associated with them, although sometimes they remain hidden. Another advantage is that electronic money cannot just disappear from the till - admittedly some will see that as a disadvantage - and it facilitates financial administration. No doubt a number of merchants also stick to cash payments because it allows them to keep their income, or part of it, out of sight of the taxman. But that is not a valid argument. Technological developments have greatly increased the ease of use of electronic payments in recent years. It is no longer the cause of exasperating traffic jams at store checkouts. Thanks to applications such as contactless payment by bank card or smartphone, this is faster than cash payments. Banks have also developed apps to make digital payments easier, for consumers and merchants. How archaic is it when shoppers first pass by an ATM to take money out of the wall, then use those bills to pay for their purchases in a store, and the merchant later has to go back to the bank with those bills to have them added to his account? It makes sense that banks still have little appetite to continue investing to maintain the outdated technology of bill vending machines. The banks are perfectly justified in pushing their customers and merchants more strongly toward digital payments and discouraging the use of cash. By reducing the number of bill machines. Or by charging fees for those who withdraw cash, even from their own account. The consumer organization Test-Achats is fighting the wrong battle by attacking the banks that do so. It is equally incomprehensible that some banks are going through the motions for this, such as Bank of the Post recently. Cashless payment is a form of progress. It is the future, it should be encouraged. Cease the rearguard action.

If we can remove one word from the dictionary it is the word ""graduate. In a world that is changing at lightning speed and increasingly revolves around knowledge and information, we learn every day. We do this in schools and universities, but equally at home, in the digital world and at work. Learning we do from the first day of our lives, in order to understand the world around us and cope with change and difference. Knowledge, craftsmanship and skills are the basis for participating in society and making full use of your own talents. Good teaching begins with a great respect for the profession and authority of the teacher. It also requires that we remove barriers to learning and continued learning and give scholars and students time and space to find their own path. Not the government, but parents themselves choose the type of education for their children. We protect the space for special schools to design their own education based on religion, belief or pedagogical vision. Every Dutchman can count on that. We are concerned about the quality of education. This needs to go up. Teachers now have to spend unnecessary time on administration, time they could be spending on their students. Declining reading proficiency is also a major concern and this is one of the biggest tasks to improve in the coming years. We are raising the bar and strengthening the quality of education, especially on core skills such as reading, writing and math. To give young people every opportunity to learn and develop, we stand for an education system in which young people are encouraged to continue learning. For those who are able and willing, moving on from MBO to HBO and on to university should always be an option. In the labor market, learning and working is a natural combination for more and more occupations. In very many professions and jobs, we continue to learn to ensure that we always have the knowledge, craftsmanship and skills needed. Science is the guide into a world we do not yet know. Our universities and research institutes are among the world's best, and we owe this position in part to the intensive cooperation between education, business and government.

We want people to be able to control their energy bills by encouraging clean energy generation close to home. No roof remains unused for solar panels. Generating your own solar energy at home will not yet cover the total energy demand. Therefore, we give space to the development of all forms of clean energy. New large-scale onshore solar and wind projects are still important to meet sustainability goals. It is important to speed up wind farm construction procedures and make them less complex. The demand for clean energy is too important to prevent with strict regulations. The solar and wind energy industries are expected to involve local residents in the arrival of solar and wind farms and to take nature into account when developing solar and wind farms. We want people to have as much opportunity as possible to generate their own clean energy. We see a role for energy collectives and neighborhood windmills. We also encourage energy cooperatives that realize local large-scale renewable energy generation. Participation and co-benefit of residents is key. For example, provinces, municipalities and the state should also be able to require that people living near a wind turbine share in the profits. The climate agreement has already agreed that we aim for at least 50 percent local ownership for renewable generation on land. We are going to further solidify that commitment with additional funding and binding agreements. For example, local residents can participate in a local energy cooperative and share in the proceeds of a wind farm. Other ways of financial participation are also possible, such as wind farm funds, bonds and resident schemes. We expect housing associations to make their roofs more sustainable with solar panels and, where possible, to green them by installing a green roof. Within the agreements of the solar ladder, we provide space for large solar fields. In addition, we encourage the development of large wind farms. By placing them together in a number of locations around the country, we limit nuisance and protect views of the Dutch landscape. We encourage space saving by putting solar panels on roofs and facades. In the Environment Act, more flexibility is needed to apply this. The installation of solar panels in new construction and renovations will be mandatory on large roofs, P&R sites, embankments along roads and other unused space. For existing distribution centers, a feasibility study should be done for a solar roof. The government is leading by example, putting panels on all its roofs where it can. In addition, we take advantage of opportunities for solar panels on water, taking into account local nature. For businesses that do not need to renovate their roofs in the near future, it will be mandatory to install solar panels on their roofs. To this end, we include ""solar on company roofs"" with a seven-year payback period in the approved measures list under the Environmental Management Act.

For owners of homes and other buildings, we make it more attractive to insulate, ventilate and purchase a heat pump, including with subsidies and low-cost loans. There will be a favorable scheme for green roofs and facades and rainwater harvesting facilities. We ensure that reliable and practical information about energy-neutral and climate-proof (re)building is widely available. We require owners of rental properties to invest in the energy performance of their homes. The bill for making social housing climate-neutral should not fall on tenants. All new home construction is gasless, energy-neutral and includes standard nature features, such as nesting boxes for birds. From the design phase, architects, installers and experts are involved to build climate-proof. We set standards for the use of circular building materials, such as recycled concrete, wood and reusable bricks. Municipalities are working with residents and businesses to make neighborhoods natural gas-free. They will have more financial and legal opportunities to do so. We bet on electricity, geothermal heat (geothermal) and heat from water (aquathermy) as sustainable sources for heating buildings and industry. Additionally, waste heat from industry can be used to heat homes, but this should never get in the way of making industry more sustainable. Where necessary, we arrange financial compensation for people whose neighborhoods switch to alternatives to gas. We ensure a level (financial) playing field for collective heat solutions. We choose the economic and social strength of regions. From green hydrogen in Groningen to sustainable chemistry in South Limburg, from wind energy in Zeeland to Foodvalley in Gelderland, from Brainport Eindhoven to GreenBizIJmond. A directing role of the national government is needed in this regard to counter regional inequality and distribute jobs and wealth more fairly across the Netherlands. We make sufficient funds available to repair and strengthen homes in Groningen's natural gas area and invest in developing the region. The policy of spreading government services across the country is gaining momentum. The Caribbean Netherlands will provide its own energy and become a pioneer in the Caribbean. We support Curaçao in closing and rehabilitating the Isla refinery, creating space for housing, tourism and sustainable economic development. Small and medium-sized businesses are the job champions of the Netherlands. These hundreds of thousands of entrepreneurs, with their local and regional involvement, play an indispensable economic and social role in society. With support and incentives for green and social entrepreneurship, help with digitalization, SME-friendly public procurement and making European cooperation easier in border regions, we are ensuring that SMEs can continue to play this role even after the corona crisis. We ensure a level playing field for small and medium-sized businesses versus large corporations. Innovative companies are drivers of the new economy. Innovations for circular economy, (bio)medical technology, digital technology, games, platforms and 3D printing have become part and parcel of our society. We encourage businesses that contribute to a green and fair economy. We do this by opening the Climate Fund to them and strengthening (European) networks between innovative companies, knowledge institutions and larger companies. Following the tobacco advertising ban, advertising for products and services that cause substantial climate damage will be banned, starting with an advertising ban on stunt offers for air travel and polluting cars such as SUVs. Energy companies should not advertise fossil fuels. As long as the main business of energy companies is fossil, all other advertising is also prohibited for them. In the coming cabinet period, we will grant the licenses for 60 gigawatts of additional clean electricity from wind turbines in the North Sea. Those wind turbines must be there no later than 2040. Solar panels and green roofs join the list of mandatory energy-saving measures for owners of large buildings. The government is leading by example by accelerating the sustainability of government property, delivering every new government building climate-neutral and investing in making schools, sports facilities, healthcare buildings and cultural institutions more sustainable. We are investing in more power grid capacity. In addition, energy conservation is essential; it is becoming an important part of decisions about new technology, digital infrastructure, building and transportation. Nuclear power plants are not an option for renewable energy generation. Building a power plant takes decades, the climate crisis does not wait for that. In addition, the construction and decommissioning of a nuclear power plant cost tens of billions of dollars, making nuclear power in no way economically viable. Not for nothing can no company be found that wants to build a nuclear power plant in the Netherlands. Not to mention the risk of disastrous accidents and the radioactive waste we would saddle countless generations after us with. As potentially interesting options for the future, we do support research on thorium and nuclear fusion.

Especially in times of crisis, you realize what really matters - in public health and also more broadly in the economy. We experienced which people do indispensable work. We are forced to think about the future. A crisis shows us that together we are stronger. And that shows the importance of public service. No resilient society without strong government. Our faith in a fair economy is being tested. Big Tech appropriates our data and uses large untaxed profits to buy up promising competitors. Multinationals play governments against each other in a battle for the lowest tax rates and the fewest protections for workers. The profits are for shareholders, the costs and risks for people and planet. Not good jobs, but low costs drive the economy. Not society, but the lowest tax rate determines the actions of corporations. Government seems infected with this logic. Not education or healthcare, but a low budget deficit is the highest good. Knowledge, power and income are increasingly unequally distributed. Between Randstad and region. Between people who benefit from technological development, and people who risk losing their jobs because of it. In the Randstad, hardly anyone can find affordable housing anymore. There are fewer and fewer jobs and facilities in smaller communities. High standards of work and environment lose out to the pressures of ever cheaper labor without any protection. Data are the new gold. We cannot afford for this crucial information to be managed by companies and countries with reprehensible norms and values. We choose an economy in which we reward what is truly of value. Good and secure work is paramount. We reward companies that take good care of their employees and the planet. Those who don't are more heavily taxed. We say goodbye to the earnings model based on low wages and precarious work. We invest heavily in education, research and the development of new technologies. We do not compete on price, but on quality. Over the past few decades, normal household wages have stagnated while corporate profits reached record highs. That's not fair. Therefore, with the Fair Sharing Act, companies give employees a mandatory bonus in dividend payments. Furthermore, we encourage the return of automatic price compensation for employees as standard in collective bargaining agreements. Employees will have more say in the company's direction. They will have the right to vote on major decisions, such as acquisitions, diversity at the top, dividend payments and maximum pay differentials between top and regular employees. Broad prosperity comes first in the national budget. It is precisely in bad times that the government invests. In this way we prevent unemployment from rising needlessly, facilities and services remain intact, and the economy and society are ready for the future. European budget rules have become increasingly complicated in recent years and gave too little room for government to play an important role in a crisis. Therefore, there will be new agreements in Europe on responsible public finances. In doing so, governments are given room to invest in a fair and decent economy with enough jobs. When it comes to investment, Broad Prosperity is paramount; not just Gross Domestic Product. In tenders, the focus is not cost but quality of work. Current competition and procurement rules are written from a sacred belief in neoliberal market thinking. In it, citizens are reduced to consumers. Those with the most economic power often pull the longest straw. Not quality, but cost is the focus. That has to change. We want adaptation of European procurement and competition rules that put people and planet first, not the market. Thus, good working conditions and sustainability requirements are also considered. Our tax system makes the economy more fair, decent and sustainable. A fair economy means that we all pay taxes nicely, because tax money pays for the things that are good for all of us. Too often in recent times there seemed to be a welfare state for big multinationals and raw capitalism for the rest. In distributing the bill of the crisis, we protect people as much as possible and place the bill on those who can carry it best: the multinationals, the wealthy, top earners and big polluters.

The Netherlands is a clean country. A country with beautiful nature, clean air and a good environment. A country to be proud of. Our Dutch landscape is unique and world-renowned. A landscape to be cherished and deserves our protection from destructive climate policies such as wind turbines and solar farms. CO2 is a nutrient source for everything that grows and flourishes. Consequently, climate policy, which is all about reducing CO2 emissions, has very little to do with nature or the environment. No one is against green living or a good environment, including the PVV. What the PVV does oppose is senseless, unaffordable climate policy. Humans are responsible for only a few percent of all CO2 in the atmosphere. Therefore, it is an illusion that humans could substantially affect climate. The tiny Netherlands accounts for only 0.35% of total global CO2 emissions: negligible. Dutch climate policy leads to a lesser global warming of only 0.00007 degrees: also negligible. Yet CO2 has been declared ""the great enemy. The obsessive, far-reaching fight against CO2 emissions now exhibits dictatorial traits. Dutch people who want to live their lives normally are made to feel climate guilt and fear of climate change in everything they do. Climate policy costs many, many billions and plunges households into the financial abyss. Climate policy is good for nothing, but it curtails our free way of life all the more radically: we are ruled by climate hippies who want us to take our homes off the gas for many tens of thousands of dollars, even though gas is the cleanest fossil fuel. They want us to drive unaffordable electric cars. They want us to fly less, eat less meat. It's all being forced on us, and that has to stop. At the same time, our land and our North Sea are being filled with subsidy-guzzling wind turbines. Trees are burned in polluting biomass plants. Pastures are being sacrificed for solar farms. Our beautiful landscape is being destroyed under the guise of a nonexistent ""climate crisis. That, too, must stop. The PVV says: we will not be lectured to by unworldly climate preachers. That is why we are putting an end to the totally radicalized climate madness: the Climate Act, the Climate Agreement and all nonsensical measures are immediately thrown in the trash. We abolish all climate and sustainability subsidies immediately. No more money for nonsensical leftist pastimes, but more money in our people's pockets. Because because of all the billions in subsidies wasted on green terror, energy bills go up and up. While households in Germany receive money when they take a gas connection, gas in the Netherlands is being made increasingly expensive. Already, hundreds of thousands of households live in energy poverty: they can barely, if at all, pay their energy bills and often literally sit on the couch shivering with cold. Energy is a basic need, but the climate frenzy has turned it into an extremely expensive luxury item. The PVV opts for a substantially lower, affordable energy bill: we will stop the money-consuming energy transition and reduce the energy tax. Homes will not be taken off the gas. We are reversing the abolition of the gas connection requirement, allowing new construction homes to once again have a trusted gas connection - to the best and most reliable gas grid in the world. Gas will no longer come from Groningen, but will be taken from the bottom of the North Sea and imported from countries like Norway, England etc. - as is already happening now. Our coal-fired power plants, which are among the cleanest in the world, remain open. Nuclear power plants are also being built that are safer than ever. In addition, we are betting on thorium.

Everyone who contributes to society to the best of their ability can fall back on protection when the going gets tough. The government has a responsibility to guarantee a basic level of social security for every Dutch citizen. This includes a well-functioning social safety net focused on income protection and support toward new employment. Our goal is for as many people as possible to be at work, rather than standing along the sidelines. In doing so, we apply the principles of flexicurity: higher unemployment benefits that go down the longer they last, simpler dismissal laws and strong reintegration into new work. In the coming years, we are committed to: More social protection through higher benefits immediately after job loss. The unemployment benefit goes up in the first few months is then phased out. As a result, the WW limits the loss of income upon dismissal and encourages people to find new work as soon as possible. Modernize severance law so that small business owners hire people faster. In doing so, the courts cannot force a business owner to retain someone who does not function or who disrupts personal relationships. On the other hand, the court can impose higher compensation after wrongful dismissal. Less risk for employers to hire people indefinitely. Employers pay less premium for people on indefinite contracts, so it pays to hire people on a permanent basis. We also encourage employers to offer more full-time contracts. Modern forms of contract such as on-call, payroll and agency contracts do remain possible to organize unpredictable work and relieve small employers. Young people under 21 will be exempted from the high WW premium for flexible and temporary contracts. Better guidance to work. We make it attractive for welfare recipients to start working part-time by increasing additional earnings limits. Those applying for welfare benefits receive an intake interview during which a concrete plan towards employment is drawn up. In doing so, we also improve job opportunities for people with disabilities, through guidance and support in the workplace and by ensuring that work always pays off. We always look at what people can do and make sure people are less likely to be written off. For groups for which the step to regular work is still too big, we ensure that help, such as sheltered work and apprenticeships, is more readily available and ensure that existing budgets within the social domain can be used more for these (public) apprenticeships. A transparent assessment system (estimation decision) for disability, more in line with practice. In doing so, we look at what people can do and are less likely to write people off. One merged and more transferable leave system for things like birth, parenthood, short-term care and emergencies, so that people can use leave in a way that suits their situation. A higher minimum wage so that working pays more even for lower-income earners. We are making sure that work pays more and that as many people as possible get to work. In doing so, we are making the existing payroll benefits more targeted. Benefits such as welfare do not automatically rise with the minimum wage, with the exception of state pension and disability. Activating people on welfare through quid pro quo. We ask everyone to make a maximum effort to master Dutch sufficiently (B1 level). We want people to participate in society and our social security is geared to that end. Low literacy is a major barrier to employment for many people. Personal attention to a welfare recipient's guidance from the municipality is essential in this regard. There will also be performance agreements with municipalities to prevent local minimum policies from creating new poverty traps. Bringing back the human touch in implementation. There have been too many examples in recent years of citizens and business owners being unfairly classified as fraudsters. Tackling fraud should not result in someone who makes a mistake being immediately labeled a fraudster. To change this, we are strengthening internal checks in implementation while reducing unclear, legal language in government communications. Improving the human touch in implementation includes an explicit focus on accessible communication, both at physical locations and by phone, mail, email and through other (digital) means.

Over 5,000 fossils found in 'Çorakyerler' in 24 years Under the direction of Prof. Dr. Ayla Sevim Erol, Head of the Department of Anthropology at Ankara University, Faculty of Language, History and Geography, excavations have been meticulously carried out for 24 years to uncover fossils belonging to vertebrate animals in the Fatih Neighborhood. Prof. Dr. Ayla Sevim Erol, AA correspondent, said that in the first years they started excavations, they encountered a very complex and dense fossil potential, but in the following years, more homogeneous and articulated fossils began to emerge. ""Stating that they found many rhinoceros skulls in the first years and that these were exhibited in Çankırı Museum, Erol said the following: ""When we entered this area in 1997, we first excavated in an area about 100 meters long. The excavations we did every year with dental tools like digging a well with a needle because the environments where the fossils were found were unfortunately very hardened clay layers, clay layers that had become very petrified or even rocks. Even the dental instruments we use in excavations do not hold up from time to time. We have fed up with dentists, we are going to buy dental tools, so we are taking all the dental tools that we know dentists don't use and we are coming to excavate because the excavation tools really don't last in the area. Hammers and shovels break very quickly."" Stating that fossilized areas are usually located in high mountainous and hilly areas that are very difficult and troublesome to reach, Erol said, ""However, the area we are working in is an area located in the heart of the city. But is that good or bad? On the one hand, there are pros, it is an area that can be easily worked, on the other hand, there are cons, it is an area that can be easily destroyed because it is located on the road and its protection is quite troublesome."" Explaining that they have carried out excavations in an area of approximately 5 thousand square meters until today, Erol said that when they first started excavations in the area, they dated the fossils up to 7.5-8 million years ago, and emphasized that the fossils of animals found in recent excavations go back to 9 million years ago. ""We may encounter a new species at any moment"" Explaining that they can say that Çankırı had a rich nature covered with forests, wetlands, elephants, rhinos, horses and predators millions of years ago with the fossils that have been unearthed, Prof. Dr. Dr. Dr. Dr. Dr. İsmail Demir stated that Çankırı has a rich nature with elephants, rhinos, horses and predators. Dr. Erol gave the following information: ""Therefore, it is a locality inhabited by a group of animal fauna dated between 9 million and 8 million years, where there are forested areas, abundant freshwater ponds and river beds, open grassland savanna environments and abundant forested areas, from the fossils of the ancestors of the horses found in large numbers, we identify 3 different ecological environments. In this context, fossil finds belonging to more than 40 species such as rhinos, horses, wild horses, hyena (hyena), saw-toothed felines and various types of carnivores as well as antelope, deer, wild sheep and goats, bison, elephants and giraffes were found. We may encounter a new species at any time in these studies. So far, the total numbered fossils in this area, that is, the numbered fossils that we can identify the species, are over 4 thousand. Apart from that, some important unnumbered fossils can also be found in other sediments. When we add them all together, more than 5 thousand fossils were found.""

Joint statement after Erdogan and Salman meeting Erdoğan then hosted an official dinner in honor of Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman. The dinner at the palace was closed to the press. The joint statement issued after the meeting read as follows: ""The sides discussed the possibilities for the development and diversification of mutual trade, facilitation of mutual trade between the two countries and overcoming the challenges, enhancing communication in the public and private sectors of the two countries to explore investment opportunities and transform them into concrete partnerships in various fields. The two sides, as G-20 members, highlighted the great economic potential of the two countries and the opportunities offered by Saudi Arabia's Vision 2030 in the fields of investment, trade, tourism, development, industry, mining, construction projects, transport-infrastructure (including contracting), agriculture, food security, health, communication-information technology fields, media and sports, and agreed to activate the work of the Saudi-Turkish Coordination Council, to raise the level of cooperation and coordination on issues of common interest and to work on the exchange of experience between the experts of the two countries. The 5th meeting of the Turkey-Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) on October 13, 2016 Referring to the Joint Declaration of the Ministerial Meeting, they emphasized the importance of the negotiations on the Turkey-GCC Free Trade Agreement. The Parties expressed their expectation to cooperate in the field of energy, in particular in the fields of oil and refining, petrochemicals, energy efficiency, electricity, renewable energy, innovation, clean technologies for hydrocarbon resources, low-carbon fuels, including hydrogen; the desire to work on the localization of the energy sector and related supply chains and the development of relevant projects in these areas. The Parties agreed to develop production and investment partnerships in the fields of artificial intelligence, digital technologies and smart cities and to encourage private sector actors operating in these fields to cooperate. The Parties emphasized their determination to combat climate change and environmental challenges and agreed to enhance cooperation in these areas. The Turkish side invited investment funds operating in the Saudi Arabian entrepreneurship ecosystem to invest in and partner with Turkish startups. The Parties agreed to strengthen and maintain the relations between the ""Turkish Standards Institute"" (TSE) and the Saudi Arabian Standards, Metrology and Quality Organization (SASO) within the framework of the cooperation agreements signed between the two institutions. Both sides agreed on mutual visits of scientists within the framework of the cooperation protocol signed in 2016 between the Scientific and Technological Research Council of Turkey (TÜBİTAK) and King Abdulaziz City of Science and Technology (KACST). The parties emphasized the need to strengthen and develop cooperation activities between the Small and Medium Enterprises Development Organization (KOSGEB) and the Saudi Arabian SME Authority (SMEA). The Parties agreed to activate the agreements signed between the two countries in the field of defense cooperation in order to serve the interests of both countries in the field of defense and contribute to ensuring security and stability in the region. The two sides agreed to enhance judicial cooperation and exchange of experience between experts in the legal and judicial fields. The Parties emphasized the importance of cooperation in the field of tourism and the development of tourism movement between the two countries, exploring the tourism potential of both countries, as well as promoting joint activities related to sustainable tourism that benefit the tourism sector and its development. The Parties underlined the importance of strengthening cooperation between national civil aviation authorities, facilitating administrative procedures for airlines' operations and increasing the number of flights between the two countries. The Parties emphasized their determination to enhance the existing cooperation between the two countries in the field of health and agreed to explore opportunities for cooperation in the field of health investments. The Saudi side expressed its gratitude for Turkey's support for Riyadh's EXPO 2030 candidacy. The sides agreed to deepen consultations and cooperation on regional issues in order to strengthen stability and peace in the region in the interests of the two countries and their peoples. Prince Mohammed bin Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saud, Crown Prince and Deputy Prime Minister, expressed his gratitude for the kind hospitality of Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan and for the warmth and affection shown to him and his delegation during their visit. Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan expressed his appreciation for the efforts to organize Hajj in 2021 despite the challenges caused by the Covid pandemic and the efforts of the Custodian of the Two Holy Mosques to serve pilgrims and visitors, and his satisfaction with the resumption of Hajj and Umrah this year, and thanked the Custodian of the Two Holy Mosques King Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saud and Prince Mohammed bin Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saud for their efforts in this regard. At the end of the meeting, the Parties emphasized their determination to continue and develop cooperation on the basis of historical brotherhood to serve the future of the region in a way that will contribute to the common interests of the two countries and their peoples and benefit all segments of society.""

Compensatory education will start after the school report cards are issued Within the scope of Covid-19 pandemic measures, in the 2020-2021 academic year, which started through distance education using TRT EBA, EBA and live lessons, a gradual transition to face-to-face education was made as of February 15. As part of the ""On-the-spot decision-making in education"", activities have continued since March 1, with face-to-face training in some places and distance learning in others. As part of the full lockdown measures taken in the fight against Covid-19, distance education was implemented on April 29-May 17. In pre-school, special education centers and support and training courses for grades 8 and 12, face-to-face education started on May 17, while distance education continued at other levels until Tuesday, June 1. As of June 1, all primary schools and kindergarten classes within schools started full-time face-to-face education two days a week, and schools in villages and sparsely populated settlements started full-time face-to-face education five days a week. As part of the gradual normalization of the fight against Covid-19 in June, face-to-face education started in middle and high schools across Turkey on June 8. Printed report cards, certificates of achievement and graduation diplomas will be given to those who request them. Due to the end of the 2020-2021 academic year, the Ministry will make report cards and certificates of achievement for students at all levels available on e-School as of June 18. Printed report cards, certificates of achievement and graduation diplomas will be given to those who request them by school directorates as of July 2. The responsibility exams, which should be held in the last two weeks of the second semester of the 2020-2021 academic year, will be held between June 21 and July 2, 2021. Following the completion of the responsibility exams, the ""I'm also in Compensation"" program, the summer break section of the 1.5-year National Support Program (UDEP), will be implemented. Applications can be made between June 21 and July 2, and the make-up education program will be held between July 5 and August 31. Students will be able to benefit from facilities and centers affiliated with the Ministry of Family and Social Services, Ministry of Youth and Sports, Ministry of Culture and Tourism, Ministry of Health, Ministry of Interior and municipalities. Details about the scientific, social, cultural, sportive and educational activities and events to be held in schools, districts and provinces within the scope of the program can be accessed at ""https://telafidebendevarim.meb.gov.tr"". The program, which includes educational activities for students, teachers and parents on a voluntary basis, will be planned in accordance with four main themes: ""physical"", ""social-emotional"", ""academic development"" and ""special education"". Summer school for those who cannot benefit from pre-school education. Summer schools will be opened in pre-school in order to increase the level of readiness of children who will start primary school in September but have not benefited from pre-school education and to ensure that they start primary school on equal terms with their peers. Limited to the 2020-2021 academic year, children who have received pre-school education can also be enrolled in summer schools in schools with suitable facilities, provided that children who have not received pre-school education are enrolled first. In pre-school education, parents' demands for full-day children's clubs can be met by opening children's clubs. Summer schools and children's clubs will be allowed to start the week after report cards are issued. Literacy screening will be initiated for students entering 2nd grade. Within the scope of the program, literacy screening will be initiated for students moving from grades 1 to 2, and according to the results of these screenings, students who are identified in need will be provided with additional lessons and additional material support. In addition, 3rd and 4th grade students will be supported through the Primary School Education Program (İYEP). Workbooks prepared for 1st-8th graders and supplementary worksheets for 1st-4th graders will be distributed free of charge in September. The Ministry, which is also preparing a critical outcomes screening for high schools, aims to open schools full-time in the 2021-2022 academic year and to provide face-to-face education.

Is early diagnosis possible in ALS? Corum Private Hospital si Neurology Specialist Uzm. Dr. In his statement on June 21, World ALS Day, Okan Delikan gave information about ALS disease and diagnosis. WHAT IS ALS, MOTOR NEURON DISEASE? Stating that ALS (Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis) and Motor Neuron Disease are generally used in the same sense in the world, Uzm. Dr. Okan Delikan said, ""The 2 groups of nerve cells of the system that makes voluntary movements (pyramidal system) are called motorneurons. The nerve cells from the cerebral cortex to the spinal cord are called first motor neurons (upper motor neurons). The electrical impulses generated in the motor center of our brain are transmitted to the spinal cord by a nerve cell called the 1st motor neuron (alpha motor neuron). The second motor neuron (lower motor neuron) starts in the region of the spinal cord called the anterior horn. The passage of electrical impulses between the 1st and 2nd motor neuron takes place through chemical processes in a space called the synapse. The electrical impulse transmitted from the synapse gap to the 2nd motor neuron is transmitted from the spinal cord to the relevant muscle area. With this electrical impulse, our muscles work. Diseases affecting the first and/or second motor neuron are generally referred to as Motor Neuron Disease. ALS is just one of the diseases that affect these nerves. The cause of the damage to motor nerves is unknown, but the disease is neurodegenerative, i.e. destructive. Many factors such as certain environmental factors such as pesticides and heavy metals, hormonal disorders, vitamin deficiency, viruses, cancer have been suspected to cause the disease, but there has not been enough evidence for any of them."" Uzm. Dr. Okan Delikan gave the following information about ALS: WHO CAN GET ALS? ALS is not a contagious disease; it can occur anywhere in the world and in people from all walks of life. It is slightly more common in men. The average age of onset is 55 years. However, it can occur at a very young age or at a very advanced age. About 2-6 per 100,000 of the population has ALS. WHAT ARE THE SYMPTOMS? Symptoms are not the same in every patient. Usually, weakness or thinning in one arm or leg is the first symptom the patient notices. For example, it becomes difficult to hold a pen, button a button, carry a bag; or the patient stumbles when walking. In some patients, the disease starts with speech or swallowing difficulties. The patient or relatives notice a lisp or nasal speech. These symptoms may be accompanied by muscle twitching, pain and cramps. There may be uncontrollable crying and laughing. WHAT ARE THE RISK FACTORS FOR ALS? Of all ALS patients, 90% are sporadic (individual) and 10% are familial ALS patients. Half of familial ALS patients are also inherited. It can therefore be said that the disease is largely unrelated to heredity. Another characteristic of ALS patients is that they fit a certain personality profile. These patients are usually intelligent, emotional and creative people who have risen in their profession. Some epidemiologic data suggest an association between overexertion or certain chemicals and this disease, but there is no definitive proof. IS EARLY DIAGNOSIS POSSIBLE? ARE THERE STAGES OF THE DISEASE? Over time, the weakness spreads from where it started to other areas, such as the muscles of the arms, legs, tongue and pharynx. The patient's activities of daily living may be restricted due to muscle wasting, weakness and twitching throughout the body. It may not work on its own. He cannot eat, dress or bathe. He may not even get out of bed. The critical period of the disease is when the respiratory muscles also weaken. The patient needs immediate and close medical support. The course of ALS is different for each patient. Although survival is usually given as 4-6 years, there are many patients who live 10 years or more. There are ALS patients who live more than 20 years with good medical and social support. The reason for this difference is not fully known. HOW IS THE DIAGNOSIS MADE? Diagnosis is based on clinical signs and symptoms. Nevertheless, the disease can be confused with many muscle and nerve diseases, so some tests are necessary. An electromyogram (EMG) performed by an experienced electroneurophysiologist is the diagnostic tool. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of the brain and spinal cord, some blood and urine tests, lumbar puncture (examination of lumbar fluid), muscle biopsy may be required, as they may be confused with other diseases. WHICH SYMPTOMS SHOULD BE TAKEN INTO ACCOUNT? The physician checks for distinctive neuronal signs including; muscle atrophy (loss of muscle volume), muscle weakness, twitching, increased muscle tone, changes in normal muscle reflexes. If the neurologist finds signs of motor neurons in at least three parts of the patient's body, a definitive diagnosis of MNH can be made. IS THERE A CURE FOR THE DISEASE? Unfortunately, there is no definitive cure for ALS yet. Nevertheless, work on new drugs continues intensively. Special medication for ALS patients is used to reduce the amount of glutamate in the body, thus slowing the progression of the disease. This treatment not only prolongs the patient's life, but also delays the onset of ventilator dependency or, in appropriate patients, the surgical opening of a hole in the trachea (tracheotomy). On the other hand, it is very important to make the patient as comfortable as possible and to provide supportive treatments that will enable the patient to lead a normal life. Today, there are many possibilities for rehabilitation of the patient. These are determined according to the needs of each patient. Drug treatments for muscle pain, cramps and muscle stiffness (spasticity), treatment with a psychiatric approach to patients and their relatives for changes in emotional state, treatment of speech problems with a speech therapist, medication for increased salivation and swallowing problems or tube feeding treatment called PEG, pain treatment, tracheotomy or connection to a respirator for the treatment of respiratory problems."" Erdoğan signed the decree, Hagia Sophia is opened for worship The 10th Chamber of the Council of State annulled the Council of Ministers' decision of November 24, 1934 to convert Hagia Sophia from a mosque to a museum. The Association for Continuous Foundations, Historical Monuments and Environment filed a lawsuit with the Council of State for the annulment of the Council of Ministers' decision to convert Hagia Sophia from a mosque to a museum. The Chamber examined the case on a hearing basis and heard the parties at the hearing on July 2. After the hearing, the 10th Council of State examined the file. The Chamber has made its decision. The Chamber annulled the decision of the Council of Ministers dated November 24, 1934 on the conversion of Hagia Sophia from a mosque to a museum. It is registered as a mosque in the title deed. In its reasoning, the State Council stated that Hagia Sophia was owned by the Fatih Sultan Mehmet Khan Foundation and that it was put into the service of society as a mosque. In the justification stating that Hagia Sophia is registered as a mosque in the title deed and that this cannot be changed, ""It is concluded that it is not legally possible to use it other than as a mosque in the foundation deed and to dedicate it to another purpose. The immovable properties and rights belonging to the Foundation, which have been protected since time immemorial, cannot be prevented from being used by the society for whose benefit they were left."""" The presidential decree was published in the Official Gazette. The Presidential Decree on the opening of Hagia Sophia for worship by transferring it to the Presidency of Religious Affairs was published in the repeated issue of the Official Gazette. In the decision, the Council of Ministers Decree No. 1934 on the conversion of the Hagia Sophia Mosque into a museum was rejected by the 10th Council of State. It was reminded that it was annulled by the decision of the Chamber. In this context, it was decided to transfer the management of the Hagia Sophia Mosque to the Presidency of Religious Affairs in accordance with Article 35 of the Law No. 633 on the Establishment and Duties of the Presidency of Religious Affairs and to open it for worship. President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan shared the Presidential Decree on his social media account with the note ""auspicious olsun"". President Erdoğan will address the nation. President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan will deliver a State of the Nation Address at 20.53 today. In his post on his social media account, Fahrettin Altun, Head of Communications Fahrettin Altun said, ""Our President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan will deliver a State of the Nation Address speech today at 20.53."" Parliament Speaker Şentop: Opening Hagia Sophia for worship is a historic decision. Mustafa Şentop, Speaker of the Grand National Assembly of Turkey, said, ""It is a historic day with the decision. The decision that turned the mosque into a museum was reversed. The opening of Hagia Sophia for worship is a historic decision."" Şentop stated that Hagia Sophia will be opened for worship until Friday next week. Russian Orthodox Church: We regret the decision of the Council of State. The Russian Orthodox Church has expressed regret that the Council of State in Turkey has annulled the decision to convert Hagia Sophia from a mosque to a museum. The judicial process regarding Hagia Sophia. The Association of Continuous Foundations for Historical Monuments and the Environment first filed a lawsuit for Hagia Sophia with the Council of State in 2005. The association had requested the annulment and stay of execution of the Council of Ministers' decision dated November 24, 1934. On June 24, 2005, the 10th Chamber of the Council of State rejected the request for a stay of execution of the Council of Ministers' decision. In 2008, the Chamber rejected the case, pointing out that there was no violation of the law in the use of the Hagia Sophia Mosque as a museum. The Council of State Administrative Appeals Board upheld the Chamber's decision. In 2016, the association again filed a lawsuit with the Council of State. The association's individual application to the Constitutional Court was decided in 2018. The Supreme Court had deemed inadmissible the application alleging violation of the freedom of religion and conscience due to the rejection of the request to open Hagia Sophia for prayers due to ""lack of jurisdiction in terms of person without examination"". Source: AA

Remarkable Message from the President of the Constitutional Court Zühtü Arslan, President of the Constitutional Court, said: ""Where the courts are unable to respond to the search for justice and find solutions to disputes in accordance with the principles of independent and impartial adjudication, it is inevitable that extra-legal searches will emerge."" A symposium on ""The Right to Respect for Private Life in the Context of Professional Life"" was organized at the Constitutional Court. Emphasizing that discussions on the right to privacy continue in many countries, Arslan said: ""In his novel 1984, the British George Orwell depicted a dystopian world in a frightening way. Orwell expressed the internalization of surveillance as follows: 'The assumption that your every sound was heard, that your every move was watched unless you were in the dark, had become an instinctive habit, you had to live with it - you did'. According to Orwell, the most effective surveillance tool of 'big brother' power is television. Technical advances that allowed television to be used ""both as a transmitter and receiver put an end to privacy"". Orwell passed away two years after he completed his book in 1948, long before the invention of the internet and smart cell phones. If he were alive today, he would marvel that the dystopian world he described in his book has been perfectly realized, even surpassed. He would probably be horrified to see the emergence of an omnipresent 'global big brother' who can monitor even those in the dark with cameras that can be found almost every step of the way in these days of the so-called digital age, who can track locations with software, who sees without being seen, who is ready and available everywhere."" Commenting on the security investigation and archive search for those who will be recruited to the public sector, Arslan said, ""This is equally valid for dismissal from public office within the framework of loyalty and devotion to the state. In other words, the state will be able to take action to dismiss or otherwise administratively sanction public officials who it determines to be in breach of the constitutional duty of loyalty. In this sense, dismissal from public office can be characterized as an interference with the right to respect for private life based on the cause and / or result due to the close relationship between professional life and private life."" Constitutional Court President Arslan stated the following: ""Guaranteeing the right to respect for private life and privacy is of utmost importance for the protection and development of the individual's material and spiritual existence, autonomy and freedom. In addition, it should not be forgotten that a rule of law in which fundamental rights and freedoms are protected and legal security is ensured is also a sine qua non condition for a welfare state. Indeed, like other sayings under the sun, this one is not new. Tunuslu Hayreddin Pasha, who was also a grand vizier for a period in the Ottoman Empire, made this determination years ago and conveyed it to us in his book. According to Tunuslu Hayreddin Pasha, who shared his observations on the institutions of the countries he traveled to in Europe in his book published eight years before the proclamation of the Constitutional Law, 'the countries that have reached the highest levels of prosperity are those that have put the principles of freedom and the constitution, which corresponds to political reform, in place'. Undoubtedly, today, as in the past, the judiciary has the greatest duty to restore the principles of freedom and the Constitution. When this duty is fulfilled properly, trust in the judiciary will rise to the desired level. Therefore, as members of the judiciary, we have to constantly review and renew ourselves in self-criticism and accounting. This is our debt of conscience to the law, to justice and ultimately to our nation to which we belong.""

Merkel pays farewell visit to Turkey German Chancellor Angela Merkel paid her last official visit to Turkey today. I also stated that the EU will continue to support Turkey in this regard. Turkey has carried out very important work on Syrian refugees and migrants. As of now, we have completed more than 60 thousand briquette houses, and our goal is to increase this to over 100 thousand.""

April 25, 1999 Silent Peaceful Protest April 25, 1999; They came quietly, sat peacefully and left quietly. April 25, 1999 marked a turning point in Chinese history. Some people with a close interest in China describe this as one of the most severe crackdowns on a spiritual development practice (Falun Gong) in modern times. Mr. Li Hongzhi, the Nobel Peace Prize nominated founder of the Falun Gong self-improvement practice, began teaching his practice to the public in 1992. Falun Gong, a completely free qigong practice based on the principles of ""Truthfulness, Compassion and Forbearance"", has rapidly gained popularity across China. However, with nearly 100 million people practicing Falun Dafa in China at the time, far exceeding the Chinese Communist Party's membership of 65 million, the Chinese government saw Falun Gong as a threat. On April 11th, 1999, Luo Gan (a member of the Standing Committee of the Communist Party Political Bureau from 2001-2007 and the person responsible for the persecution of Falun Gong), under instructions from the Tianjin University magazine, made severe accusations against Falun Gong. In response, Falun Gong practitioners traveled 120 km to Tianjin and held a demonstration to peacefully explain Falun Gong. Their aim was simply to tell the truth, but the state met them with severe violence and arrested 45 people. After the incident, practitioners demanding the release of those arrested were told: ""We cannot help you here."" Since Tianjin is under the central government in Beijing, practitioners were directed to Beijing. After that, many Falun Dafa practitioners went to Beijing on April 25th, 1999. Practitioners wanted to go to the National Appeals Office to demand the release of detainees. However, practitioners who were received in Beijing by Chinese State Security authorities were directed to the gate of Zhongnanhai, the seat of government, via two separate routes. One of the interesting things was that there were many cameras on the streets that day. On that day, instead of the usual police presence, a large number of soldiers with rifles were waiting in the vehicles, ready and waiting. It was as if they were waiting for an instruction. Falun Gong practitioners were also waiting-they waited for 16 hours. According to Chinese security expert Ethan Gutmann (Nobel Peace Prize nominee), state security forces wanted to set a trap for Falun Gong practitioners in government territory. They had worked on a scenario and through this scenario they were going to create a bloodbath. The appeals office never opened that day. Falun Gong practitioners waited calmly. Eventually, then Prime Minister Zhu Rongji met with the five petitioners and promised that those arrested in Tianjin would be released. The practitioners then dispersed in silence. On April 24th, 1999, 10,000 Falun Gong practitioners gathered to petition the Beijing Appeals Office, but were directed by security forces to the Zhongnanhai Government District. (Photo: Minghui) However, the Chinese Communist Party later called this incident a ""siege of government territory"" and used it as the biggest excuse for the unthinkable persecution of Falun Gong that began on July 20, 1999. At that time, Falun Dafa practitioners were banned from going to school, so a Falun Gong practitioner could not enter university. Practitioners were thrown out of their workplaces and prevented by the state from taking their place in society. Falun Gong practitioners were imprisoned, tortured and killed. April 25th, 1999, a peaceful protest followed by a massive genocide, dubbed 'A Black Spot in the History of Humanity'

Banned Social Media Platforms in China Since the 1990s, the use of internet has become widespread in the world with the introduction of web2.0 based systems. Thanks to this system, which enables people to interact with each other via audio and video, the whole world has started to be aware of each other. The Internet has created a new communication environment called ""new media"". Moving from a passive to an active position, users communicate with the world by producing content on virtual communication platforms such as social media, news sites and blogs, independent of time and space. The differences in the political, economic and technological situation of countries also show differences in the use of new media by their users. Social media platforms, which are used in many countries around the world today, are not used in some countries. Social media platforms such as Facebook, Twitter and Youtube are banned in some countries. North Korea, Iran and China are among these countries. In the People's Republic of China, ruled by the Communist Party of China, new media is driven by the ruling CCP. Despite bans and censorship on internet use in China, internet usage is quite high. This is because the CCP has developed its own alternative social media platforms to replace the widely used social media platforms such as Google, Twitter, Facebook and Youtube. The reason why China does not use these outsourced social media platforms is that the servers are located outside China and are out of China's control. In other words, the CCP has banned the use of social networks whose source is outside China and which it cannot control. As of 2018, there are approximately 1 billion internet users in China, with a population of 1.4 billion. A study on New Media Practices in the People's Republic of China has yielded some interesting results. According to the research conducted by Bozok University Faculty of Communication, the Chinese media, which is under the control and pressure of the Chinese Communist Party in terms of freedom of expression and press freedom, as well as social media, are closed to the outside world. The Chinese equivalents of some of the world's most widely used social media platforms are as follows: Google - Baidu, Twitter - Immomo or Weibo, Youtube-Youko, Facebook-RenRen, Watsapp-QQ, Wikipedia- Baidubedia. The CCP has also closed the Chinese market to foreign companies, with bans imposed to protect national security, silence dissenting voices and control the population. The world's biggest companies such as Facebook, Twitter, Youtube could not enter the Chinese market. Although Google maps was open in the early days, it too was blocked after Taiwan was recognized as an independent country. This is because although Taiwan is an independent country, it is seen by China as a dependent country of China. In the research, it is stated that despite all these bans, people living in the country mostly use Chinese social networks, but they also use Google through virtual private networks such as VPN. When these are detected, a number of legal penalties are applied. Looking at these and similar surveys, it leaves a question mark on how much the people living in China are aware of what is happening in the world. Semra Sener, Epoch Times Turkey. 100th anniversary of May 19th The date of May 19, 1919, the first step in the struggle for independence, is being celebrated with enthusiasm all over Turkey on its 100th anniversary. Mustafa Kemal Atatürk sailed to Samsun on May 19, 1919 on the Bandırma Ferry. This special day, which was declared Youth and Sports Day, was celebrated for the first time in Samsun in 1926 under the name Gazi Day, and became official in 1935 under the name Atatürk Day. Atatürk dedicated this holiday to the Turkish youth. History of May 19 After the First World War, there were poor living conditions for the Turkish nation. Mustafa Kemal Atatürk landed in Samsun to think of a remedy for a nation that had lost hope. For this reason, the journey starting from Istanbul on May 16-19, 1919 symbolizes liberation. Samsun was a strategically important and reliable gateway from the Black Sea to Central Anatolia. This was a salient point for the occupation forces. The British landed troops in Samsun on March 9, 1919. In response, Lieutenant Hamdi of the Turkish Machine Gun Company took the soldiers and went up the mountain. Mustafa Kemal Atatürk arrived after the British High Commissioner complained that the Turkish people were taking up arms and it was decided to send a trusted commander to the region with extraordinary powers. This was a great opportunity for him. When Atatürk arrived with his team of 18 people, the view he saw was not encouraging. There were British occupation forces in the city. The people were not in a position to protect themselves. The sleepless nights spent on the road were now to continue. May 19, 1919 was the beginning of the process that began with these steps taken by Atatürk and led to the Republic of Turkey. ""When I saw Samsun and the people of Samsun, I once again strongly believed that all my thoughts and decisions concerning the country and the nation could be fulfilled. The patriotism and sacrifice that I read in the eyes of the people of Samsun, which I saw in their state and situation, was enough to lead my hopes and imaginations to a positive belief."" -Mustafa Kemal Atatürk- Nationwide Celebrations May 19 Youth and Sports are being celebrated with enthusiasm all over the country. Especially in the squares of big cities, big events are organized. Marches, exhibitions and concerts are organized in many streets and squares of Ankara, Izmir, Antalya, Çanakkale, Bursa, Bursa, Istanbul, Hatay and especially Samsun. Some of Atatürk's Words to the Young People of Our Country: ""You are the young sons of the new Turkey! You will follow me even if you get tired. Those who decide to walk without rest will never, ever tire."" Mustafa Kemal Atatürk said: ""Young people, you are the ones who strengthen and sustain our courage. With the upbringing and culture you have received, you will be the most valuable example of human values and love of homeland. O rising new generation, the future is yours. We founded the Republic; it is you who will raise it up and maintain it... My humble body will one day be grounded, but the Republic of Turkey will live forever."" Mustafa Kemal Atatürk I am addressing the Turkish youth, especially the youth of today and the children who are growing up. The West was far behind you, the Turk. In meaning, in idea, in history this has been said. If today the West is finally showing technical superiority... O Turkish child! And that crime is not yours, but the result of the unforgivable negligence of those who came before you. And let me tell you, you're very smart! That's obvious, but forget your intelligence! Trump Meets with Falun Gong Practitioner Survivor of Chinese Persecution WASHINGTON - Falun Gong practitioner Yuhua Zhang, persecuted for her faith in China, was among 27 survivors of persecution for their faith who met with US President Donald Trump in Washington on July 17. Before fleeing to the US in 2015, 59-year-old Yuhua Zhang had been repeatedly imprisoned and persecuted in China, for a total of 7.5 years, for refusing to renounce her faith. The Falun Dafa Information Center has repeatedly claimed that hundreds of thousands of followers of Falun Gong, a meditation practice, are being held in prisons, labour camps and brainwashing centres, where the vast majority are being persecuted into renouncing their beliefs. The White House said President Trump met with Ms. Zhang and four others who have been persecuted in China, including a Tibetan, a Uighur Turk, and a Christian, as well as religious persecutors from 17 countries, including North Korea, Iran, Pakistan, and Burma, to reaffirm his administration's commitment to religious freedom. Ms. Zhang's attendance at this event marked the first time that a Falun Gong practitioner had met with the highest-ranking official of the US nation in an official meeting. As they gathered around President Trump in the Oval Office, Ms. Zhang told President Trump that her husband, a Falun Gong practitioner, was still being held in Suzhou prison in Jiangzu province. ""Forced organ harvesting is still going on, so we must take action,"" Ms. Zhang told President Trump, adding, ""Words are useless."" Ms. Zhang also told Trump about another practitioner who was imprisoned in the same place and died the day after his release. He added that this practitioner vomited a lot of blood before he died. During the meeting, President Trump said, ""All of you have suffered quite severely because of your faith."" ""Each of you has now witnessed the importance of promoting religious freedom around the world,"" President Trump said. US Ambassador Sam Brownwick, the US Ambassador to the International Freedom for All Faiths, announced that the US administration will announce ""additional measures"" to its efforts on religious freedom at a conference on July 18. Secretary of State Mike Pompeo and Vice President Mike Pence will address this topic in their speeches at the event. Persecuted persons were in Washington, D.C. to participate in the Resolution to Promote Religious Freedom event hosted by the U.S. State Department. The three-day conference, held from July 16-18, is the most comprehensive event on religious freedom in the world. Falun Gong practitioner Dr. Dr. Gong, who survived the persecution in China. Yuhua Zhang delivers a speech at the conference on the Decision to Promote Religious Freedom at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs on July 17, 2019. (Samira Bouaou/The Epoch Times) The Quest for Justice. Ms. Zhang, formerly a professor at Nanjing University, told the conference on July 17 that she had been subjected to severe torture during her detention in China. He added that the torture included electric shocks, sleep deprivation, forced injections of unknown drugs and running for hours in the scorching sun. Ms. Zhang's husband, Zhengyu Ma, an engineer, is currently serving a three-year sentence in Suzhou prison for sending a letter to the regime's top leaders urging them to end the persecution. Ms. Zhang has not heard from her husband since 2017. ""I think about my husband every day and every night,"" Ms. Zhang said at the conference, fearing that her husband may have been tortured to death like thousands of Falun Gong practitioners. She worries that many Falun Gong practitioners, whose numbers are currently unknown, may have been killed for their organs. Ms. Zhang reiterated in her speech that, based on evidence from various sources, it has long been alleged that the Chinese regime has been killing imprisoned Falun Gong practitioners for organ transplants. These claims were confirmed in a report published in 2006 by independent researchers David Matas and David Kilgour, who argued that this was happening on a much larger scale than previously thought. Last month, after a year-long investigation, an independent court confirmed allegations that forced organ harvesting is taking place on a ""serious scale"" in China. The resolution stated that Falun Gong practitioners are the main source of organ transplants. Ms. Zhang, who has worked tirelessly for her husband's release since arriving in the U.S., called on the U.S. government to impose sanctions under the Global Magnitsky Act on Chinese officials who ""carried out illegal arrests, torture and killings of Falun Gong practitioners."" Ms. Zhang also said, ""Many of the people involved are still serving in China, and many have been promoted for supporting the persecution of Falun Gong practitioners."" ""I believe that the U.S. government, international media and human rights groups can help free my husband and hundreds of thousands of other innocent Falun Gong practitioners who are imprisoned,"" she concluded. How does the Wood Wide Web work? The forest is a social environment for trees. Trees are also social beings. There are trees that help each other. Trees spread their roots underground with fine fibers to find moist ground in the soil. In the process, they mate with fungi. Trees that are close to each other communicate through their roots and branches. But fungi play an important role in the communication of trees that are not close to each other. Mushrooms can easily penetrate into the soil with their reticulated structure. Trees also send signals to each other through fungal networks in their roots. Even in rainy, stormy weather, they send news in this way, albeit slowly, regardless of the weather. They have a very slow electrical speed of 1 cm per second. Mushrooms work just like a fiber optic internet network. With their thread-like structure, they move easily deep into the soil. A single mushroom can bind an entire forest together. These fungal networks are like a forest internetwork. (Wood wide web forest internet network) Trees that lose this communication network often get sick. Fungi are living things that fall between animals and plants. The cell structure of fungi sets them apart from plants. They have cell walls called chitin, which plants lack. This makes them closer to pests. Fungi do not photosynthesize like plants. Fungi owe their existence to the organic bonds they form with other living things. Fungi can spread over large areas with their underground cottony webs called suckers. In Switzerland, there is a thousand-year-old honey fungus spread over an area half a kilometer wide. Another mushroom in Oregon is estimated to be 2400 years old and is said to weigh 600 kg, covering an area of 9 square kilometers. According to this, fungi are the largest living organisms in the world. Fungi are not always friendly to trees. They search the forest for edible tissue and kill trees. Fungi are living things between animals and plants. Every tree has to expand its roots to get food and water from the soil. For this, each tree works with the most suitable mushroom species. There are plants that can spread without the need for a fungus, but fungus-powered trees can take up more nitrogen and phosphorus. For example, the oak tree works with oak cork. The fungi attach to the hairs on the roots of the tree and spread where they are found. From there it can spread to other trees. It partners with the corky structures of other trees, thus forming a corky network. It is through this network that trees are able to share food among themselves or receive information about pest attacks. If they cannot find food, they die. They ask trees for a third of the sugar the tree has in exchange for their services. Fungi can help trees by attracting heavy metals from them. They remove some harmful bacteria. Air pollution could spell the end of mushrooms. Some trees of different species compete with each other, while others feed each other. Beech trees, for example, are said to be able to be friends with others. Trees don't want to lose their friends. This is because the disturbance of gaps in the forest affects the air humidity balance. Especially trees grown for commercial use need plenty of space. These trees should get a lot of sun, photosynthesize and grow quickly. When trees are too close together, they can interfere with each other's use of sun and water. pixabay. Vanessa Burche, a student at the University of St. Achen, discovered that beech trees help each other even when they are in different places. The tree with more sugar gives it to the tree with less through its roots. The strong help the weak and make each other equal. Beech trees communicate through fungi and carry out a kind of social cooperation. Usually foresters cut them down because they think that trees should not be too close to each other. But a beech forest in Lübeck, northern Germany, with dense stands of trees, yielded too much. The trees fed each other better when they were close to each other. It is also difficult for trees to defend against insects in places with spaced trees. This runs counter to the evolutionary theory of survival of the fittest. Because the health of trees depends on them being together. When the unhealthy and frail ones disappear, gaps appear in the forest and are vulnerable to the weather. The heat and sun pierce the soil of the forest and disrupt the humid cool climate. Even seemingly strong trees get sick from time to time. If there are no other trees nearby, even a light insect attack can shorten their lifespan. To Be Continued...
